title: Good app with room for improvement
body:
This is a very cute app, easy to set up and very helpful. 
There are a few points that would need to be improved for me to be fully on board with this.
The price of the subscription is very expensive. The app itself is quite inflexible, you need to pick exact days for all your habits instead of just “twice a week” or “once a month”, which makes it harder to use for ND people like myself. It feels way too rigid. I also can’t figure out how to go back to a previous day. Sometimes I go to bed after midnight and am unable to check my habits for the day.
Finally, the notifications need to be more customisable. I would like to get notifications with my habit but it gets buried under all the notifications I get for friends visiting, finch going on adventures, daily check ins etc. I would like to be able to turn off the notifications for the game parts while keeping them on for habits. As it is now I have had to turn off all notifications.
All-in-all good app!

title: Too much change
body: I will give it five stars because it is a fantastic resource but I do wish the devs would listen a little more sometimes. My main issue is that the self care element is getting more pushed aside as the gaming side of the app is built upon. First, we lost journeys despite an overwhelming number of people finding this unhelpful. It meant you could work towards bigger rewards over longer periods of time and it didn’t rely on having streaks. You could get a reward for 75 days of brushing your teeth without it having to be in a row, or so many times in a week. It was accumulative and this helped people see their progress without losing motivation because they didn’t get a streak. Then we stopped getting asked to rate our mood on the opening screen. Some people didn’t like this but it could’ve been made optional. Now, a lot of people report forgetting to log their mood. And finally, the activities section has become more hidden. It used to be on the front page. Now you have to go searching for it. Those are just some of my observations. I do like the app but I feel it doesn’t hit quite the same for self care as it used to, and I now use it more as a tamagotchi with goals attached than a habit tracker.

title: Finch is such a wonderful app!
body:
Finch is honestly one of the most comforting and encouraging apps I’ve ever used. 💚🐦 It makes taking care of yourself feel less overwhelming by turning even small everyday goals into something positive and rewarding.
My little Finch has become such a special part of my routine. Whether I’m completing goals, reflecting on my day, or simply checking in, the app always feels encouraging and never judgmental. It reminds me that small steps still count and that I can be proud of myself for the things I accomplish.
I also love how cute and personal everything feels, from going on adventures to collecting items and watching my Finch grow. It makes self-care feel fun while still being genuinely meaningful.
Overall, Finch is so much more than just an app to me. It’s a comforting little space that encourages me to keep going, celebrate my progress, and be a little kinder to myself. I’m really grateful to the people who created it. 💚

title: I loveee finch it’s perfect!💕✌️👑
body:
Okay, so Finch is basically like having the cutest, fluffiest personal trainer who happens to be a bird. And honestly? I'm obsessed.
You adopt this adorable little birb (yes, BIRB)—mine is called Cosmo, but you can name yours whatever you want. Fun fact: I originally named mine Rose, but I changed it to Cosmo because it just matched the vibe better! Set your daily tasks, check them off, and watch your feathered buddy grow and go on the most random adventures. There are SO many different countries to unlock—you have to unlock them one by one—and Cosmo has been to Paris and Scotland so far. They're literally traveling the world while I'm getting my life together!
The customization is amazing. You can deck out your birb in outfits like tiny wizard hats or superhero capes, and you can even change the colors of specific areas like the beak, wings, feet, and head. But here's the thing—the body (like the stomach area) stays the same color you chose at the beginning forever. So if you pick blue at the start, that's your birb's body color for life! But heads up—pretty much everything costs rainbow stones, the in-game currency! Outfits, color changes for those specific areas, sending your birb on holidays, editing their house—it all needs rainbow stones, so they can get pricey!
Your birb goes on adventures for hours at a time, and when they get back, you actually get to chat with them about their trip! Plus, they evolve from a baby to a teen and beyond as you keep up with your goals. Oh, and get this—your birb can even have their own MICRO PET. How adorable is that?!
Seasonal events keep things spicy, you can add friends to share the journey, and the daily streak system is weirdly addictive in the best way possible.
But here's the real magic: Finch makes you actually WANT to do your self-care tasks. It's like having a supportive little companion cheering you on. What's not to love?
Download it. Thank me later. Your future self (and your adorable birb) will be so grateful! 🐦✨

title: A nice app, but it doesn’t take into account users with disabilities
body: I like this app a lot. It’s very cute and it keeps me on track. However, when you first start up the app, it asks you if you have any health problems, like mobility issues. I have mobility issues, so I clicked that on the app, ever since, the app has been suggesting that I do things that I’ve told it I can’t do, and the events where you can earn rewards are quite unsuitable for me. I opened a new event just now to see that it’s suggesting things like “go for a walk,” or “have a solo dance party.” The app already has information on me that says that I can’t do these things. I’m not sure why the developers haven’t taken this into consideration and haven’t given those who can’t do these tasks their own list of things that they can do. It’s a really nasty feeling to open up an event and see that you can’t engage with it. It’s a nasty reminder of how much different things are for you.

title: Definitely recommend but-
body: I first downloaded finch about 2 years ago,it helped a lot but due to storage I had to delete it. About 2 months ago I downloaded it again and it was helping even more since I was in a really bad pit of depression. It recently logged me out and when I tried to log back in it said everything got deleted so I had to restart. Restarting is something I hate that makes me insanely stressed and more overwhelmed and I usually hate the thing I have to redo. This isn’t helping at all anymore and now I just have a resentment towards finch. Though I absolutely loved this app and it helped a lot,it forcing me to restart with no perks even though I had the 3 day free finch+ has just made my mental health drop a little. Definitely recommend this app if you’re fine with the possibility of having to restart!!

body: I love the app, even if i don’t do most of my goals, i try my best, and help fix up my routine for the better, and to help my mental health. I didn’t think this would be helpful but it actually is when you have the mindset to change, and if you like keeping you up a streak and also want to care for your little Finch Companion. I just wish there was more to do with our Finch though, like play some small games like ‘guess which cup it’s under’ or ‘don’t say the same thing as me’ (example: ‘Tomadachi life’ has it with their Mii’s, i know it’s a mental health improvement app and don’t want to take things from other people, but i think it would be cute to play little short games with our Companion, so we can built more of a friendship, and to get gems or energy to level up. title: Finch review-WARNING-LONG
body:
My name is Rosie Driver and I am 10,11 in September and I have had finch for five days so this review may not be accurate in other people’s point of view.

Before I got finch,I was a mess,not completely finishing tasks and only doing half of everything!I had everything written down on the notes app and had too do extra by deleting the crosses and ticks,but now I don’t have to do any of that,I just have to wait for the next day for it to do it manually.

The reason I gave 4 stars and not 5 is because unless my finch comes back from and adventure or I finish a task I don’t go on the app,so I think there should be mini games to earn some gems or even a new currency! I think you should also take a pic or video when you are doing a task to prove you did it,since you are able to claim it if you didn’t actually do it!

Thank you for taking the time to read my review,I’m sorry for how long it is and have an amazing day,bai!

Ps.if the creators are reading,I love this app and please reply

title: Honestly too stressful
body:
I downloaded this to try and get little dopamine hits from doing things I should be doing, to help me do those things. I liked it at first. However, maybe the app started out quite simple but for a new user coming in so this point all the different quests, sub-quests, side quests, adventure quests, do this for a micro pet, do that for a new doormat etc are very complicated to find in the interface and it doesn’t make it clear where you have to go and what you have to do and GOODNESS my job is stressful enough as it is, I don’t need more pressure on me for tasks I don’t even know why I am even worrying about! It’s like the Duolingo owl all over again. Just too much for me I’m afraid. 

Also just a warning to anyone concerned about IT security- the ‘Questions With Friends’ part of the app looks a little bit like profiling/data harvesting to me. Ask yourselves why they are collecting this data and what they’re going to do with it.

title: Why change things that aren’t broken?
body:
I used to really enjoy Finch, but one recent change has made the experience noticeably worse.

Previously, when you got a micropet egg, the app would prompt you to choose which goal to link it to. This was simple, intuitive, and fit perfectly with Finch’s supportive, guided style. Now, that prompt is gone, and you have to manually dig through the bag section. 

It might seem like a small change, but it makes a big difference. It’s less obvious, more time consuming, and easy to forget, especially for an app that’s supposed to make self-care feel effortless. The old system felt encouraging and user-friendly - the new one feels hidden and unnecessarily complicated.

For an app built around gentle motivation and good habits, removing helpful prompts like this feels like a step in the wrong direction. I really hope the developers reconsider and bring back the automatic prompt or at least make the feature more visible again.

title: Great so far for ADHD/OCD
body: I really, REALLY struggle to get up and do anything. Basically, i download Finch because I can’t get up and do anything. Seriously. I can’t for the life of me start anything and that applies to anything from writing or art (which I love to do) to personal hygiene tasks. Finch has given me some of the motivation I need to get started. I think body doubling is so helpful and Finch helps me with the more mundane (albeit not easy for all of us) objectives. I get up, I brush my teeth, wash my face, do something I enjoy, and go to work. These all may seem like minor things, but they’re not. They’re things that I struggle with (or did struggle with much more than I do now). I think Finch makes me take a little more accountability. It’s great. If you’re struggling, it might not 100% for you, but try it!! Why not?

title: Self Care
body:
I’m afraid that you lost me because of the timing of certain things.

Before I even experience the app there is the push to get a special offer on the price. I’d like to see just what it is all about before paying & because I want to do so, I’m being rewarded (?) with the message that I have irrevocably missed out on saving money. Next you want to access my friend list - hey, I’ve still experienced nothing but hatching an egg & answering some questions and I’ve missed out on a special unrepeatable offer so do I trust you yet? 

The ad & review made Finch sound wonderful but you’re alienating me. My anxiety is soaring & wanting to access my contacts now feels like the final straw. Remove app time.

I’m aware I may have missed out on something wonderful, if the reviews are to be believed, but you’ve missed out on my cash.

Maybe wait a day or a couple of activities before you grasp for cash & contacts to also tap for cash. Give us a chance to feel that you mean well & might be helpful.

I know it says ‘self care’ but it would be good to feel that you also care about us too & not just what you can get out of us straight away.

title: Reminders for a busy mum
body: I love this app! It has helped me, as a busy mum with suspected ADHD, keep up with small habits that I would usually forget about. I originally downloaded it some time ago and never got into it, then eventually managed to get into the habit of opening it. Once you get started, earning money for dressing your finch and decorating their home provides great motivation to keep checking in and keep sticking to those goals. It allows you to pick new goals regularly. This means if you are going through a difficult time, you can stack up easy wins, like just taking a shower. But equally, i have the opportunity to challenge myself a little more when i can, like the spring cleaning challenge in March. Really grateful for this beautifully designed, well thought-out app. Feels like it was made for me!

title: Finch review
body:
Amazing, fantastic app. But I do have a few minor suggestions that would really improve it: 

1. The ability to design their home more freely. Currently there is set positions and furniture but you can choose the design. I think it would really help some people who want to be a bit more creative with it if we could choose where things go. I understand that this is one of the additional features and not the main point of the app but I think it would be worth adding. 

2. More interactive features. I think there is a lack of interaction with your finches home. It would be really cool if we could have something like if you tap the bed, then your Finch will sit in bed. Or if you tap the dresser, it will reveal all of your outfits. This would really help to make players feel more immersed in the game and like there are there with their Finch. 

3. Making micropets more interactive. Maybe having an extension later in the game (eg. when you have fully grown your Finch) it will give you the opportunity to unlock a garden that you can decorate with outdoor furniture from a new shop to feed, play and take care of your micro pets. Giving animal lovers the opportunity to feel like they have a pet even if they don't own one in real life. 

I think some of these changes would really improve gameplay and give players more responsibility over their finches life and bring out the creative side of people who maybe didn't know the even had one. 

Thank you so much for reading this and I hope you have a wonderful day. 😁❤️

title: I love finch!!!!
body:
Over the past few years, I have been struggling with anxiety. Finch is an amazing app and I totally recommend it, for anyone who needs a push. Once you install the app it asks you if you want finch plus, which I have never bought. Then you will have to complete a quiz all about you. Once completed it will give you a personalised goal list for the day. Once a task is completed you earn energy for adventures and gems for the shop. In the shop you will find 4 categories:
•clothing
•furniture 
(Both of these have a main shop and a section with rarer items that refreshes every day)
• colour
• travel
You can also take educational tests, listen to soundscapes, breathing exercises, yoga, and a daily review. 
After trying app after app after app finch is the only one that has had an impact on me as a person , my anxiety and how I deal with situations.Please don’t dismiss this app because it Is amazing!

title: Finchin Fantastic
body: I love this app so much. I go on it at least three times a day, maybe more. It catalogues not just your progress but if you are doing all you can for yourselves to help you with mental health. You have cute pets who have cute micropets, they learn things daily (at 52, I have learnt so many new things too) they travel too so it’s global learning sometimes. You keep to routines to keep yourself busy or you have the option to do nothing if your issues call for that too. It teaches you how you treat yourself in comparison to how you treat others, helping you recognise toxic patterns of behaviour that you are displaying and change what you can to better yourself. This app has helped me more than you know and I will continue to use it. There is part of it where you can journal how you feel, it keeps it safe too, knowing you can offload things and not hold negativity and it goes away so you don’t keep reading and repeating that negativity. The things it helps with are numerous and all you do is look after and nurture your cute tiny bird to grow and learn in a really cute game. Building a home and safe space. There is nothing finer and it can be for so many age ranges. If you need to help yourself get or keep healthy physically and mentally, I highly recommend this app. You are important and this app and your finch bird help you realise that and the goals you can reach when you invest in you. Thank you to the creators of this incredible app 💕

title: Can’t Stress How Vital This App Was For My Mental Health
body:
I suffered from a serious bout of burnout and depression. Desperate to even get out of bed, I downloaded this app. From the UI and UX alone, this app CARES about you. It’s so personal, indepth, adorable. I even have a bit of maternal instinct for my little pet because the app does such a phenomenal job. Like?? My pet was 0.7 centimetres tall when she was a baby. What. That’s adorable. Of course I’ll get up and go to work if it makes her happy. Whatever my little daughter desires. 
Genuinely life changing though, and now i’m at a top university in my country and it is no underestimation to say this app helped me get there. The developers have my heart and soul.

title: A Cute Idea That Tries a Bit Too Hard
body:
Finch clearly comes from a good place. The idea of pairing self-care with a little virtual pet is charming on paper, and it’s easy to see why it appeals to some people. Unfortunately, in practice the app leans so hard into “cute” that it becomes twee to the point of being almost condescending.

Everything about Finch — the language, the animations, the tone of encouragement — feels more like it’s aimed at children than adults. Tasks are framed with excessive cheerfulness and overly simplified affirmations, which can make genuine self-reflection feel trivialised. Instead of feeling supported, I often felt talked down to, as though complex emotional states could be fixed with a sticker, a smiley face, and a cartoon bird telling me I’d done great.

For people who already find self-care difficult or awkward, this kind of presentation can be actively off-putting. Rather than lowering the barrier to entry, the saccharine tone risks pushing people away entirely — reinforcing the idea that self-care is fluffy, shallow, or not meant to be taken seriously. Ironically, it’s exactly the sort of approach that can make people bounce off self-care rather than embrace it.

Finch will undoubtedly work well for some users, especially those who enjoy gamified positivity and a very gentle, childlike aesthetic. But for adults looking for something that treats their mental health with a bit more nuance, maturity, and respect, the app may feel more patronising than helpful.

author: Flissycattt

title: Get this app!
body: I was recommended this app by a fellow neurodivergent friend and I cannot recommend it enough. Suddenly tasks that I had negative associations with and felt like a slog I’m now looking forward to doing because I’ll get rainbow stones and get my little finch a new piece of clothing or furniture. As silly as it sounds it feels so good seeing progress day by day and I’m feeling better in myself because of it. I’ve also got my 5 year old involved and she’s now excited about doing chores because she gets to get stuff for finch. 10/10 recommend, it would be great if they made a kid/parent option somewhere and it would be great if they maybe added a housework section with chores in like laundry, doing dishes or loading unloading dishwasher and another tab for work rather than it all being under productivity with only vacuuming and tidying in there, but being able to create your own goals is a good work around. Also it would be so cool if they made it possible to have daily/weekly/monthly/annual goals, I’m on the premium free trial but can’t see anything like that. Either way this is an app and wonderful way of shifting your mindset if you struggle doing daily mundane tasks.

title: Good
body: I’ve had finch for almost a year now and it did help a lot at the beginning, but I tend to struggle with keeping up routines as they sometimes feel like a pressure. I do love the whole watching your birb grow up aspect, and the house design and choosing outfits, and it’s lovely to watch her grow up and develop her personality. The things that could improve this app are changing the monthly themes so I don’t feel stressed or like I have to go into the app every day to get the reward instead of going at my own pace. This part basically just makes me spend more time on screens, but it’d be great if the pressure was gone. Though I do recommend this app as it did help me with morning and bedtime routines for quite a while even if I don’t spend much time on the app at the moment.

title: Made such a difference!
body: I never leave reviews but after using this app for a week I can say that in a short time it’s really helped me get out of the slump I was in. I was struggling to get out of bed tbh but just having the to do list on this app really helps me, particularly for the evening/bedtime routine too - which is so important to set yourself up for the morning. I’ve been able to get out of bed when the alarm goes off every day this week which I haven’t done in months. There’s def a little dopamine hit when you tick off a goal but I feel like it’s a much nicer and positive hit than what the dreaded doom scrolls give. I’m a 90s kid so of course v reminiscent of tamagotchis too, which is lovely. If you are struggling with self care motivation I really do recommend giving it a go - there is nothing to lose and a lot to potentially gain.

title: I love Finch
body:
I have never had a more helpful self-care app. I downloaded this app in late 2022 out of curiosity. It helped, but I was already quite a productive person and didn’t really need an app to keep me on track. In 2024, I hit a depression. My life flipped and I needed something to help me. I spent every day rotting away on my phone and some days didn’t even leave my bed to shower. I got better, but depression doesn’t just go away. A year later, around August this year, I was low again. I searched everywhere for a self-care app that could just help me, even a little. Finch came to mind. During my first week, I found the app to be silly, just something entertaining to get me through simple tasks. But now, as seasonal depression is slowly starting to arise again, this is my favourite app on my phone. 

You can set as many tasks as you want, set notification reminders to complete, and get a cute little bird. And all for free! There’s even little features that I find to be adorable. For example, if you set your mood to ‘Bad’, I found that the energy I get from tasks (set to 5) goes up by 2 (to 7, for me) which is such a considerate detail because knowing when you’re low, it’s harder to get these tasks done, so you get a little bit more of a reward for doing them.

Thank you to everyone who worked on this app and still works on it today. Sometimes, that little bird is the only reason I get out of bed.

title: Best app for my ADHD
body:
I have struggled with sticking to lots of “productivity” or “ADHD” support apps that help build habits and keep me on track. This one really worked for me. Probably the fifth type I have tried. 

I have stuck with this consistently. It has helped me keep to my brain training, diet and exercise routine. It has helped improve my relationship and reduce my anxiousness. It has helped me be more productive and more focused on my work and writing. It has helped me consistently improve my mood and led to me be accepting in saying when I am happy. 

I am keen to see if the gamification continues to evolve: will there be greater customisation in the bird design, the furniture and (more importantly) the ability to add my own affirmations that appear in the cycle or that I can choose which ones to appear. I did wonder if sub-tasks would be good but I sometimes overcomplicating things actually make things worse. The design is probably aimed at a younger audience so interested to see if there is chance to see an older variation (although this feels like when books are re-published with a different cover to let adults read them without embarrassment when they should just own what they enjoy). 

I think this is worth the money and the good works that they do. I do think it is easier when you get this app with someone you know. It was my best friend who recommended it and that has made a huge difference for me sticking to this too (despite the fact we never actually mention it we just send each other good vibes).

title: Great app! (awesome for helping my silly little adhd brain get tasks done)
body:
This app has genuinely helped me with quite a few goals, especially when it comes to drinking more water and remembering to actually socialise with the people I love, something that I sometimes forget to do due to ADHD and the meds I’m on.

Currently have a 209 day streak! (Go me!!) and am really loving it

Thank you to the creators of this app and to the person who recommended it to me ( a good friend of mine ) for providing a tool that’s both fun and useful in a way that never feels condescending or awkward. 

I’ve tried somewhat similar things in the past but always ended up dreading udon them by the end since it felt like it was shaming me whenever I messed up, whether that be true or whether it was just in my head via the wording, but finch NEVER makes me feel like that! It never makes me feel guilty for not completing a goal or for my goals being too simple, and actually encourages having simple goals on days that are difficult as to not end up getting burnt out.

That, as well as having the option to pause streaks for when you’re busy or just can’t handle using it at that time, really helped when my grandad passed as it was difficult to do my daily finch during the organisation of the funeral and such, but when all that was done I was able to go right back to it with no problem, and was able to write down my feelings on it and get a little reward for doing so!

Something as silly as the idea of receiving a fun little hat or a new rug for my little bird friend can end up getting me to take care of myself, and honestly I think that’s just what I’ve needed all this time.

(Though as a suggestion, it would be pretty cool to have more complex goals as an option for organisations sake, such as multi-step goals or the ability to link goals to each other and that being a way of getting more points? Sometimes I’ll end up with an easy goal and a complex goal and both will give me the same amount of points which always feels off 😭 might just be a me thing though and I’m sure the team behind it have reasons why this may not logistically work anyways haha)

title: Actually unbelievably helpful
body:
I sometimes find it kind of dystopian that there are apps to digitise pretty much everything, but I was astonished to discover how goddamn useful Finch is for self-care and literally changing your life (slowly, habit by habit). I downloaded it on a whim after a friend’s recommendation and it helped me very significantly to overcome depression at the start of the year. Now that I’m (mostly) out of it and using the app less as a crutch and more as a tool for self-improvement (exercising, reaching out to friends, cutting down on bad morning habits), I also think they’ve perfected the balance of motivating you without pressuring you to complete the goals you set. I’m very grateful that this app is free.

(I have one very nitpicking request for the next update: there seems to be an error in the Galápagos window design (I own the blue one). Unlike the other window/door designs, it always shows the outside as blank white light regardless of the time of day. It’s otherwise such a lovely design - would be great to see this fixed.)

title: Invaluable for improving mental health
body: Finch helped me getting through a bad bout of depression. What I particularly like about it is, that you can do as much or as little as you can cope with at different stages of your mental health journey. There are pre-defined goals you can choose to try and achieve each day and they start with little things like "get up for 10 seconds" - not such a little thing when times feel really bad. There are lots of quick aid tools and support available and you can even buddy up with someone. There is no pressure to have to achieve as much as possible and nor overwhelming. Would definitely recommend to anyone going through hard times and want a little support pet 🙂

Thank you to the developers for creating such a superb app!

author: anna-maee

title: Self care but not
body:
Finch is an interesting app. Yes it has positives, gives you the ability to put in things you want to achieve on the daily. Makes you feel responsible for a virtual bird so you have to keep doing it. As weird as calling guilting someone into doing things so a bird is happy a self care app is, I can see the charm and how it would work. 

This app is probably better for people who are severely depressed or have social anxiety issues. I’ve enjoyed my 120 days but when I’m actually living life, going out with friends, doing chores, spending time with my family. I forget to check the app. And weirdly, it punishes me for that. Breaking your daily streak, telling me it’s ok to miss a day. Where in reality I was actually more healthy in that day as I wasn’t glued to my black mirror. 

Crazy

Also seems to train you in believing that buying stuff makes you happy. “You’re missing out on these cute clothes for your finch unless you pay us £70 a year”

Kind of repetitive once your finch is an adult. Also they grow up way too quickly. 

However, it is a well designed app, good features, nice ux, with no ads. Which is good they haven’t sold out on that front. Though it is very expensive they do support people who can’t afford the plus which is also kind of them. 

I think these apps are patching holes of a much bigger problem.

title: Amazing app, please read
body:
My Mummy had seen an advert for the app and we both bought it. My Finch, Cheesecake, has helped me so much because I don’t just use the app for self care, I use it for jobs as well! I love the adventures Cheesecake goes on and it’s so cool that you can travel to different places, such as Rome in Italy where my Finch is travelling to right now. I have a few ideas of what you could add to the app:

•you could make it so that you can feed Cheesecake yourself 

•add more affirmations 

•make it easier to get your first Micropet 

So, they were just suggestions and other than that it’s a brilliant app. I’d give it 10+ stars if I could!!! Please make more apps like this one because it’s amazing and I think everyone should have a Finch in their life, so here’s a big thank you to the Finch team, the people who are reading this and, most importantly, a big thank you to Cheesecake. title: I love finch! One thing though
body:
I really love finch I use it daily and although I’m still getting used to it and trying to do my goals if I’ve actually done them I still think it’s a fun cute way to get things done I do have one thing this might sound silly but if I’ve had a bit of a tough day for example it’s rained my bag broke ect and I rant about it in the rant zone or another place I just dislike when it says *name of finch* got energy and will be back 10 minutes sooner! Especially after an irritated or sad rant I think it would be nice if it said something like your feelings are valid ! Remember you matter or something like that and maybe with the energy thing as well? Regardless if you add this or not I’ll still use finch because I love it!!

Edit:
I’ve found a new app and it has the same problem so I’m still looking for another. Finch turned into something obsessive you know? “For my finch oh no for my finch” and the cycle repeated. It ended up not helping my mental health but making it worse in the sense that I was becoming attached to pixels and feeling guilty if I left it/ lost my streak. Realising that wasn’t a healthy mindset is a game changer. If finch is your cup of tea that’s great but it isn’t for me anymore due to the way I felt when having it. And I’m changing my review to 2 stars.

There are breathing exercises and other self care tools to help with panic attacks and sleep. I love the reflections and gratitudes where I can write about something positive, it helps me really tune in to the things that have gone well and the people that have helped me. There is so much about this app that helps but mostly I love my birb. I’ve not missed a day yet and it’s definitely down to wanting to check on my pet. I wish I could afford to do the plus because I think it would be totally worth it. I recommend this app to everyone. It’s so helpful and I’m feeling more positive overall.

title: Love this app.
body:
I was given the recommendation to try this app by my sister. 

and I’m glad I took her advice and downloaded it because I now use it at least once a day and it makes me want to get things done so that I can tick them off and see my pet discover new things and grow up a little bit more each day!

I also really appreciated how when I was filling out the questionnaire at the beginning and it came to exercise etc I was able to select the option that said that I had a condition that limits my ability to exercise.

I really appreciate that as a disabled person because I’ve had to select things like “other” in the past when using different apps.

And whilst I don’t mind doing that it was very nice to see that Inclusive touch built into the app from the beginning.

I’m just over a week into my Finch journey and I’m looking forward to the future.

Keep up the great work Finch team. 😊❤️

title: AMAZING, I LOVE!!!!
body:
This app is truly amazing, i absolutely love this app. I first saw this app being advertised online, and I thought ‘why not have a look at it’. As I REALLY needed something like this, I had been struggling with major anxiety and feeling awful about myself and feeling constantly overwhelmed. I had a look at it on the App Store, and it looked quite good on how to deal with anxiety. In my opinion the advertising looked  quite childish, so I was a tad bit nervous when I decided to download it. I shouldn’t have wooried tho, as although some people may say it’s a tad bit childish, i find it quite soothing and enjoyable. I think that while that characters and background effects may seem a bit immature. I love it and brings me back memories, and it REALLY helps me with my anxiety and helps me feel good about myself. However I do think that if older adults are using the app there should be a different version there, as they may not be grateful for the cartoon characters and joyful backgrounds. Other than that I absolutely love this app and will be using it forever and ever. Love!!!

title: AVOID
body: This time last year, Finch was the only good self-care app available, but now they’ve taken away the one feature that set it apart from the rest and added mandatory features that are actively triggering to a lot of users. The devs stopped listening and started lying to users via email. Communication is beyond poor, timing has become exploitative, and the justifications offered simply don’t add up. I was ready to subscribe and become a Guardian before all these changes, but sadly I can no longer recommend Finch to anyone. (This used to be a five-star review.)

title: Disappointed
body:
I have really been enjoying this app. It got me doing tasks and lovely self care things. 

I decided to try the free trial and the app said very firmly “don’t worry we’ll remind you before the free trial is up”

I was finding the app so useful I was considering paying for the upgrade. But suddenly I got a notification from the Apple Store of having paid £70 without any notification from the app. I checked notifications on my phone and the messages on the app and I had nothing. 

Now I can’t enjoy using the app because I feel like I had that choice taken away and was deceived to get money. 

Given that this is something tailored to ADHDers who are likely to forget to cancel free trials without a reminder, it feels really dishonest to me.

title: So beneficial for my ADHD
body: This app has honestly been a game changer! I don’t even have the premium version but I am blown away by the incredible features that I have access to free of charge. It helps me check off small tasks through the day, so that they are easy to keep track of while also giving me that little dopamine kick of making my finch happy and earning points. I know that for me, consistency is difficult with the small things. I am able to reach deadlines (mostly through last minute stress induced panic) but finch keeps me on track with taking care of myself consistently and mindfully which makes everyday anxiety so much easier to manage. I feel proud of myself at the end of the day when I see all of the little things I did and it has greatly helped my general mental state and well being. Being reminded and keeping track of daily and weekly tasks like drinking water or changing my sheets on a Sunday, prevents me pushing things back or forgetting what I have and haven’t done but also holds me accountable to do things bit by bit to prevent a build up of stress and overwhelm. I would highly recommend finch if you want to improve your productivity and mindfulness in a consistent, doable and maintainable way that is also fun! :)

title: This app has changed my life
body: I downloaded this app when I was in a depressive episode 6 months ago. I have since used it everyday to achieve my self care and productivity goals and it has benefitted me in so many ways. You can input any goal, big or small, or choose from their suggestions to get little rewards for your bird friend by completing your tasks. There is 0 judgement in the app, so much encouragement, the ability to connect with others and send motivational messages, and an amazing range of resources and tools for looking after yourself. It took a while for me to discover the full features of this app because it is so layered and there are so many possible ways to use it! I can honestly say this app has changed my life - it has improved my confidence, my motivation, my view of myself. The fact that almost every feature of the app is available for FREE is mindblowing. Thank you so much to the devs, thank you so much to the guardians! Download this app and spread the word, there are so many people who can benefit from this and the world needs to be made aware of this beautiful community and its resources.

title: So cute!
body:
I never really had anything that made me want to start this app, except my friend saying how cute it was! 
I started it and here are a few things I really love about this game:
-There’s a streak you can optionally keep up, and if you miss one day you can rebuild it
-It has little mindfulness activities which can really help if you’re having a bad day
-It’s so cute! You can give your little Birb some clothing, decorate its nest (house), and get micro pets for your Birb!!!

Overall I really recommend this, whether you want an app to help with mindfulness or just a cute app!

title: Finally, a goals, lists, affirmation App That Actually Works for Me!
body:
If you’ve ever struggled to find the perfect to-do list app—one that’s motivating but not overwhelming, structured but still flexible—you’re not alone. I’ve tried so many productivity apps that either felt too rigid, too cluttered, or just plain boring. But Finch is different.

This app makes self-care and productivity feel like something I want to do, not just another chore. The daily check-ins, goal-setting, and gentle encouragement from my little bird make tasks feel more manageable and even fun. Plus, the ability to personalize goals, track habits, and reflect on progress really sets it apart.

That said, Finch isn’t for everyone. Some people might find the app’s cute, nurturing approach a bit babyish. If you prefer a super minimalist, no-frills task manager, this might not be your style. But if you need a little extra encouragement and a more interactive way to stay on top of your goals, Finch is absolutely worth trying. It’s helped me build better habits, stay motivated, and actually enjoy using a to-do list for once!

title: Just a tip to the developers.(:
body:
Love this app so much, I have AuDHD & this setup helps me to remember things I have to do daily, and some of the goals help me feel better when I’ve had a bad day (write one positive thing abt today (I gave it an otter emoji)), I tried the free trial and loved it, being able to choose which emoji goes with which goal is easily my favourite feature, and the most helpful somehow, it helped me to actually want to do the goal;
Which is why I think that it should be a free feature, it makes the goal feel more personal, & I can relate it to an emoji that I feel represents the goal for me, it makes my brain want to do it more than if it were just a list, or an impersonal emoji, somehow.
I would pay the subscription just for this feature, but I can’t afford it right now.):
This feature also encourages me to add more goals, and without it I don’t want to add more goals bc the golf emoji it gives is not something that encourages me to do it, I want to either delete that goal or hide it at the bottom of the list and never tick it.
I tend to enjoy relating my goals to animals or other emojis in that section, and having the emoji there helps with motivation.

Another suggestion is to make it so that when you make a goal to be ticked off multiple times, you can add a different time to be notified for them. I have a goal to eat a meal, set so I can tick it twice, it would be helpful if I could get the app to remind me for lunch and then again for dinner.

Other than that though, it’s a very helpful app, me & my friend have both very much enjoyed sending our Ashy & Cleo on adventures and giving advice on whatever they find; and sending gifts to each other and sending like 10 vibes to each other a day.

Sorry for how long this review is, but I hope it’s helpful, to both developers & people looking to get this app, I definitely recommend.(:

title: take some time to read if you want!!
body:
Ok, so occasionally I struggle with making sure I have time for myself-I have a lot of things going on at the moment already. I’ve tried various other self care apps, but I just give up on them over a while and I can’t be consistent with going into the apps, checking off my tasks and all that stuff. 
I was with my friend one day and she showed me her finch (called Lavender). She told me how she had been saving up these things called rainbow stones to make her birdhouse look better and buy her better outfits. I thought it was funny how much she cared about a virtual bird but I downloaded it anyway.
I named my pink finch Michi. I originally meant it to be called Mochi but it autocorrected to Michi so I thought “I’ll change it later”. 
I never did. 
Every day when I get home, I always look forward to seeing what Michi has discovered on her adventure. I love buying her new clothes and items, seeing how my friend’s finches are getting along too. We always talk about them. 
My parents love hearing about Michi as much as I love finding out stuff about her. They love the little things like the weight measurements (michis currently a mighty 10 grams) and especially her adventures since she’s in Sydney now.
It’s a bit silly how much I care about a finch. But really it’s more than a finch. 
Thank you for creating this app❤️

title: transformed my life
body:
I am neurodiverse, so I have a whole bunch to stuff to deal with and no structure to my life. My life used to feel so overwhelming, I felt like I barely stay above the surface. 

I've been using Finch religiously for about 4 months now and I was so happy with it I purchased a year subscription. It really gives a structure to my day and healthy clicking dopamine (i disengaged with social media now, and my screen time used to be 8-14 hours). The app is user friendly, kind, simple to use. 

The Dream breathing exercise literally knocks me out in 5-15 mins, and my brain usually doesn't do it. The cat purring soundscape is so cute and calms me down during the biggest stressors. I am learning to recognize more emotions and that really untangles the overwhelm. I'm writing more, I reflect more, I am kinder to myself. 

I log in all of my activities during the day (as you'd schedule them in the Sims) and it gives me a sense of accomplishment and restores my confidence. My confidence used to be so weak - I felt like I couldn't do anything and I'm always drowning in things to do, but it's simply not true. 

I have a better understanding of my needs and my abilities, I accomplish more, I manage my life admin better and overall, I'm just much happier. Using Finch literally transformed my life for the better.

title: Autism and mental illness
body:
I am autistic and have mental health issues and finch has been one of the very few apps I have found really helpful. It took me a few times of downloading it and forgetting about it but now I’ve got it into my routine I’m remembering it every day and it’s given me a space to rant about how I feel, reflect on my emotions and things that happen and set myself goals to keep myself going. 

I really struggle with my memory and executive dysfunction so having things to remind me and rewards in the app to encourage me really helps and I’ve found it helpful that there isn’t any skipping tasks or buying gems as this means it actually encourages me to keep on top of tasks as it’s the only way to move forward. 

It’s also super cute and I love the representation in the app with mobility aids (though I would love them to add a power assisted wheelchair or any wheelchair especially a pink one)

title: Grateful 🫶🏾
body:
I got finch properly 2 years ago but because of my experiences with mental and physical issues it was hard to accept help and commit to this app. Just recently though I've been consistent with this app and it's helped me to recognise things about myself and to allow and be open to help. I've been using it for the mood tracking, reminders and techniques. I love how there's no pressure on having to do it and have a little penguin buddy is fun that you can dress up, send on holiday and also have my friends on it so we can encourage each other with small things you can send. Little did I realise by helping this little penguin and being on it consistently it has allowed me to help myself and also take the attention away from me through this buddy. I've been living through this penguin and I love how I can set things on my own terms with what I'm ready to do. Took me a while to figure it out with possible autism but once I have it's been so helpful. I even suggested it to help friends and it's a get assurance to check in for all of us and has taken the pressure of what a friendship must look like.
I also love how there's a community for it on discord and Facebook. I've always struggled with relationships with people so it's nice that there are people who understand how it's like to be mentally and physically unwell and share our experiences, and to encourage each other in our own journeys without judgement or pressure. It's allowed me as a young person to make mistakes, learn and grow.
I don't know where I'd be without Finch, it's saved me on numerous occasions and I love how feedback is always listened to. It's been affordable and worth every penny once I was actually able to afford but I love how you can sponsor on it, I got lucky enough to try and loved the pick me up. It's nice that it's like we're all in this together and being part of a team. It's encouraged me also to feel I can give back someday when I am well enough and I even told my support workers about it for their clients to use and to suggest it as an easy little thing. I look forward to seeing how it grows more and am grateful for the team continuing to change the world and make awareness for self care and mental health. It's also a bonus you can have a widget and  that makes how my iPhone display is look even better. Just thank you for saving my life and for helping me stay in tune with who I am and how I'd like to be, while still being allowed to be vulnerable in a safe space of my own accord. I will always be grateful for Finch

title: Helped me so much
body:
I was diagnosed with ADHD and GAD (generally anxiety disorder) this year. As well as having Pcos, so to sum it up I’m forgetful, sensitive, anxious, mood swingy, unmotivated but also motivated and the list goes on. 

I’m currently on two types of medication to help with the adhd and gad, I downloaded this app just to test it and see what it’s like, this app has done nothing but help me and keep me going, I no longer forget things as much as I can rely on the app to keep it there for me and to remind me, it makes completing boring things fun which motivates me to carry on. I’ve been having some trouble remembering to take my medication but this app has helped a lot to remind me everyday to take it which is so so important. As a neurodivergent queen this app has just been amazing. I love it so so much and recommend it to anyone who struggles to do basic things like I do. 

I hate to admit it but I struggled and still do sometimes with getting out of bed, showering, brushing my teeth, washing my hair, taking care of myself, washing my clothes and other things that everyone else seems to be great at… 
finch has definitely helped a lot in that aspect with getting me out of bed and doing things I don’t want to do as it feels like I’m getting rewarded for doing so, getting the lightning bolts which is almost like getting money so I can spend it on making my pet and her room really cool, I love animals as well so it feels as though I’ve formed a connection with my pet which makes me want to go on the app everyday just to check on her and see her as it makes me happy, it sounds weird but in reality it’s just so comforting. 

I’m currently on a 67- day streak with finch and I’m so glad I found this app when I did!

Thank you 🙏

title: Can we make Daily Streak optional please?
body:
I have found this app so incredibly helpful over the past few years. It has pulled me through moments when all I could do was brush my teeth each day. 

I do need to give some less positive feedback now though. 

The new daily streak feature, while motivating for some, can be incredibly off putting for me.

When I’m motivated it can occasionally be useful (though it fundamentally feels click-baity). When I’m unmotivated or depressed, though (aka when I need the app the most) it feels like negative reinforcement. Another telling off I don’t need.

Over the years I have really appreciated the the app’s gentle approach, but this feels like a cynical add on. Something designed to keep you coming back to app day in day out.

I understand it’s probably useful for you to track usage, but it’s incredibly depressing to see Finch become part of the click-bait machine. 

Can you please think about making this newer, and arguably less functional, feature of Finch optional?

title: ADHD lifesaver
body: I have tried SO many apps to help me manage my ADHD and this has been the only one that really works (and makes me feel good about myself while I use it). The novelty of the new month events keep it interesting for my brain that gets bored easily, and the reward for completing a task and energising my little bird Juniper helps me regulate dopamine so much better! Needing to energise her first thing so that she can start her adventure is my favourite feature as it motivates me to look after myself in the morning (when executive functioning is hardest)! I love the reflections too (much more achievable for me than writing a journal entry) and the fact that all the key features are included in the free version. It really feels like this app was built with care, kindness and understanding and I feel so grateful that it exists, thank you 💖

title: Life changing app
body:
I’ve been using this app for 120 days now and it has truly made a difference in my life. I don’t use mine so much for self-care but for motivation to complete boring household chores. For years I have been overwhelmed by the state of my house, never sure where to start and just letting mess and dirt pile up because I couldn't seem to get my act together. I started by just putting some small daily tasks on the app (such as cleaning the sinks, wiping the kitchen sides, cleaning the toilet, removing old food from the fridge etc) and I have never been this consistent in my life. As time has gone on I’ve added bigger weekly tasks such as reorganising my cupboards  or deep cleaning a room and my house has gone from being somewhere I’m ashamed to invite people round to, to somewhere that I know people could drop in to at any moment and I can feel a sense of pride. All because of a little virtual bird. 
Genuinely brilliant app with endless opportunities for someone to improve their lives. I wish I’d discovered it sooner.

title: Surprisingly effective
body:
A friend suggested this to me and I new that I’d initially enjoy it and make use of it but I thought as per usual I’d become distracted, bored and forget it existed. Surprisingly I’m quite far in now and finding it stop very useful and compelling. I have adhd and very much struggle to motivate myself to do many tasks, with a bit of setting up I’m now finding I’mactually still doing things I’d normally have given up eg eating more veg with my meals, drinking more water and such.

It works on the principle that you set yourself daily tasks which by completing you earn rainbow stones which are effectively the in game currency. You use these to buy room decorations, clothes and later on can buy other things like different colours for your finch and locations to visit. You also can connect to friends finches and send them things like hugs, compliments and so on through the day.  There’s also useful journeys which are groups of tasks that encourage you to do certain things eg feel more positive, eat more healthily and such. These contain suggested tasks but you can also add your own. 

As with anything you could frig the system if you wanted, earn lots of rainbow stones without actually doing anything but ultimately the only person you’d be cheating is yourself. The paid option goes towards keeping the app going for everyone (why I paid) and does unlock a few more slots in the randomly populated shop plus you get more seasonable achievements and some more task customisation options. However it’s very good even as a free version. There’s also an option to apply for a guardian to sponsor you paid membership if you can’t afford it, which are generous people who pay extra per month so others can get more out of the app. There’s a few bonuses for this but nothing significant, it’s more about the desire to help other people. 

Overall this app is very much about positive mental and physical health and taking care of yourself, and you get a cute bird (and little pets for it) to help motivate you

body: I used to love this app but they added guilt to it. They now require you to say how long you will commit to looking after your bird. It used to be guilt free. Had a very stressful busy time caring for an injured relative and when I came back I thought I would use the app (which I had the paid subscription for) to try to take care of myself a bit. Now it says, "How many days in a row will you look after (your bird) for?" I emailed them to ask them to provide an opt out to this and they said, "as there are unfortunately not any current plans to remove this screen - so sorry for the inconvenience!" As a neurodiverse person I DO NOT NEED MORE THINGS TO FAIL AT. You destroyed your USP, now it is the same as every other rubbish habit app. I've deleted my subscription, my poor bird is dead.

title: Best app on my phone
body:
I found Finch through a comment within a FB book group I’m in and after the first hour of being on Finch I became
1. Obsessed 
2. Productive and
3. Focused. 

I’ve had Finch for almost two months now and I’m still obsessed. It quite literally changed my life and I’ve never felt more proud of myself for pushing through procrastination and avoidance. Which was something I battled with on a daily basis. 

I’ve tried many habit tracking, gratitude, journal and self-care apps before and I always ghosted them after some time due to a lack of purpose. Finch gives you that purpose! It rewards you for doing the bare minimum - LIVING! WAKING UP! NAPPING!

You can tailor it to however you see fit, no matter the goal, and it rewards you with rainbow stones so you can purchase cute items for your little birb. Who, by the way, gains a fantastic, witty, compassionate and awesome personality as you whisk them away to destinations in search of adventures. It truly is ADORABLE! 

Who knew looking after a cute little birb that you can dress up make your life so much better! It’s like Tamigotchi got a massive and superior upgrade that you actually want to care for and doesn’t unalive if you neglect it! 

Thanks Finch team for creating this incredible app. You’ve no idea of the insurmountable positive impact you’ve made on my life!
💜💜💜💜

title: Certainly made a difference
body:
I’ve been using this app for 9 days now and I absolutely love it. I am 27 years old and suffer with chronic nerve pain which is worsened by any movement so, ofcourse, it’s easy for me to want to avoid moving altogether. My pain is so intense that I live on morphine and, both the pain and medication, cause me to suffer with anxiety and depression. I mean, who wouldn’t get depressed when they’re in constant pain?
Before finch, there were days where I’d wake up and think ‘nope, not today’ and just go back to sleep. Since finch, I’ve done my best to achieve atleast some of my daily goals- for example, one is to go outside every day (even just to sit in the garden for 5 minutes). Finch allows you to set goals that are completely personal to you. You don’t need to set a goal of running a mile everyday…you can set a goal as small as washing your face every day. It’s just perfect and it really highlights the fact that every achievement, no matter how big or small, is important. 

Finch has helped me so much. It’s really given me the motivation I was lacking to achieve small but realistic goals every day. I love the fact that there are goals you can choose from or you can make up your own (for example, doing a 10 minute walk is something I can’t do so I edited this goal). I also love that if you wake up one day and think ‘I really can’t achieve one of my daily goals today…’ you can just skip it until another day.

The motivation you receive is from your birb growing up, your birb going on adventures, and the fact that every goal you achieve gives you rainbow stones. Rainbow stones are what you use to buy furniture for your birb’s home, clothing/accessories for you birb, and dye colours to change your birb’s look.
I’ve recently joined the Facebook group for other finch users and have made many new friends already, which is just lovely.

In summary:
Finch is a super sweet app and very easy to personalise and adjust to suit every individual. 

Note:
It’s not a criticism as such but there’s only one thing I would add- I wish we could play mini games with our birb. I’m currently having a bit of a low day today and although I’ve used various SOS resources on the app, I feel like I could do with a little mini game of some sort. Perhaps a distraction section would be a good idea. You could include mini games that you play with your birb, games you play with friends (but you could do it so it’s not super time sensitive, you just take it in turns to play), you could have a section full of positive quotes/phrases, an organising section (for example, some organising minigames like the Tappy app are great for anxiety), you could even add a way to properly chat with your birb (I know there is currently a way to have a quick chat where you reply to something your birb has said but it would be nice to have a proper conversation- like the Replika app).

Overall, on a scale of 1-10, I would give this app a 9 purely because although I’m super happy with it and haven’t found anything I dislike about it, I do feel that it has lots of potential for more to be added/included.

title: Incredibly disappointing, hidden scam!
body:
The app isn’t bad, but DO NOT commit to the plus feature in any way, especially not the free trail! 

I took a free trial with the “plus” feature, after trying, it just wasn’t for me, so went to cancel it and noticed the subscription was not there? I thought okay strange but that’s fine, it must just not roll over. Clearly, I was incorrect! 

Not only did they then go on to attempt to charge me £39.99 for a plus subscription that I couldn’t cancel (also was not in my App Store app so could not have been an active subscription), they tried to also take £69.99 in additional to the other payment, so £110 in total!

They tried this multiple times without me ever having the option to cancel and the payments kept getting declined. What’s worse? I would go on to the app and have the plus subscription as an immediate pop up because, according to the app, I did not have an active subscription!! 

I get paid this morning and at 2am this business successfully took £110 off me for one subscription that I wasn’t even being given the option to cancel! I certainly never subscribed twice?? How would that even happen? I then email at 11am on a Friday morning and immediately get an out of office response stating ”our support team is available from Monday through Friday, 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM EST. If you’ve reached out towards the end of the day on Friday, it may take until the following Monday before we’re able to respond.” Obviously, I don’t consider 11 o’clock in the morning (which is actually 6am EST) to be “towards the end of the day”. 

Overall I’m just so so disappointed. I have never experienced an app blatantly steal. The app wasn’t bad, it just wasn’t working for my needs so I didn’t want the plus subscription, and on top of not allowing me to cancel by not even showing that I have an active subscription, they have taken triple the money I would have ever committed to spending even if I did (£39.99).

title: Amazing self-care app
body:
This app motivates you to help yourself. It has a simple game and task based approach to help you celebrate the little wins every day, and takes a lot of research from cbt, mindfulness, psychology and makes it really accessible for children and adults.
It reminds me of the old tamagotchis, where you do tasks to help them grow. In this case you do things which help you and your inner child grow, getting a healthier dopamine kick.

The journeys are really good - say you want to improve your fitness, simple unfailable goals like 3 press ups. Or you want to improve your relationships? Schedule notifications for a games night or a catch up.

Really excellent.

title: Great app for self care and mental health
body:
Finch is a great app whether you are just looking to keep up with daily goals, a place to reflect on your day, or feelings, or if you need some help with your mental health. 

I initially downloaded Finch as I was looking for an app that I could keep a record of how I was feeling throughout the week. However recently I have been struggling with anxiety and this has helped me to stay on track with routine tasks and identity how I’m feeling. There’s breathing exercises and a ‘first aid kit’ that have helped me on bad days and stopped me from spiralling. 

The app gives a sense of accomplishment once you have completed a goal , even when if it is a small one, and I have found to be really useful in helping me stick with daily tasks for longer that I would have otherwise.

I have struggled with other self-help apps and not been able to stick to them. I have found there is a lot more resources (anxiety/feeling quiz, breathing exercises, reflection areas, exercises and soundscapes.) It’s a great idea for a self help app and amazing how a little bird can make a difference.

We and all of my mates have it. It is a great way to have fun with friends and family, help if needed, pass time and be a reminder. 
Me and my mates all grind the game whenever we can. Waiting for something, in a car etc, relax and chat with friends.

You can dress your pet up, experiment with house decor, help you breath, remind you to (brush your teeth, go to bed, brink water etc). It is the best app I have downloaded and I can’t stop playing it. 
It will bring a smile to your face. 
Also, make sure when going through the introduction you read it to choose the colour of your pet. I ran through it and got grey (the colour I wanted) but if you want to have an opinion on colours, take it slow. 
(When your pet is a toddler, colour can be changed, but it will take some time).

title: Helping
body: I really love this Finch app. I’m a sufferer of depression, anxiety and seizures which gives me very little energy or motivation to do the things that would be considered ‘simple’ and ‘basic’ life skills. Finch makes it easier because of the gentle and motivational push that’s needed to achieve these goals. I enjoy having my virtual pet (Bubble) and it’s actually a nice bit of comfort to be able to talk to Bubble and share feelings that I wouldn’t be able to share with a human. It’s also nice to not feel as lonely as I normally do as anxiety stops me from stepping out of the house. The only thing I really wish was that it was a cheaper price for the added-benefit subscription. Being disabled, out of work and living on the breadline, it’s too much to fund the full version. However, I’m thankful to have my little virtual friend in my life ☺️

author: nathsgj

title: Love you finch <3 🥰
body:
I have been using finch for just over a year now and use in my everyday life! My long distance partner shared it with me so we could send each other good vibes and thinking of you messages and hugs and stuff however I absolutely love the app and use it for all it’s functions!

The free version has plenty of content enough to still be functional and rewarding and does not cause frustration like with other free apps I have used… and at the same time, the payed version is really worth its value and has a lot of awesome bonus features, and the Guardians feature to gift a membership for those in need is such a lovely thing, I love these kinds of supportive and inclusive communities and is also great for under 18s without a bank account who don’t want to ask their parents for a subscription, parents won’t allow them or can’t afford. Thank you finch team for making it available for everyone 🥰

I love how the goals are set up so that they give you a reminder but do not harass you lol I struggle with motivation a lot and sometimes someone constantly pestering me to do it makes me not want to do it anymore, and also linking the in app activities to goals helps to engage you more in all the features of the app. 
There are sooooo many lil activities available for self care, productivity and relaxing, I still find new ones to this day and find them really useful. Customising you lil birb makes logging on and completing goals rewarding, I love collecting the outfits and furniture and the season events are a great way of adding new stuff and keeping users engaged.
Adding friends is a great way to engage with people, remind yourself to check up on them and also spreading awareness and being open with your friends about mental health and the struggles of life.
Finch is for sure THE BEST wellness app I have ever encountered (and I’ve tried a lot) it has kept me engaged and offers the most helpful experience and community 😌

A couple things I would like to mention to the team…
Firstly, I preferred it when the activities tab was a thing of its own and quite obvious but now since the major layout update it is tucked away in the top right corner of home and I often forget about it, I feel it should be made more prominent to encourage users to use it and also for new users who may not find it and discover the apps full potential.

Secondly, I would LOVE ❤️❤️❤️ a feature where users can customise their First Aid Kit to add specific actions and goals maybe in a specific order so they can walk through the steps of calming down using methods that work for them as an individual, for example… I would want to put on a soundscape and do a breathing exercise first, after that to write a rant, then reminded to drink water as that pulls me back to the present and do a “managing your triggers” deep dive and finish with a meditation timer. Those are the things that work for me and other people will be very different, I am autistic and the reason I would log my mood as poor would be because I am stressed out or having a meltdown and some of the things in the current First Aid Kit don’t work for me however someone else who struggles with depression might be feeling down or depressed and need something else catered to them. 
Please, please, please 🙏 finch team can you make this a thing 🥺 I would absolutely love it I wrote this review specifically to suggest this it would really help me and a lot of other people 💕

Thank you SO much Finch team 🥹 I love you all and you 🫵 reading this, yes, I see you there 👁️👁️ ty for saving lives, you are all heroes to me 🥰

The idea of ‘micro-pets’ is amazing, and the options in the game for clothing and accessories are so cool! You can dress your pet however you want, and can even travel to different places. I’m currently travelling through Tanzania, learning new facts along with my own pet! I simply can’t recommend the app enough, it is so well designed and is absolutely amazing.

Thank you so much!

author: LOEscap

title: Amazing for AUDHD x
body: I’ve accomplished a lot today, maybe it’s cos I took my 40mg elvanse today.. or maybe I just sat around and thought about things long enough that I found a path to make a difference about how I feel about the feeling my life is collapsing around me. But I know I started small, using this app.. and I finally feel like I am rebuilding my life and reshaping my daily habits, little by little. With the help of my cute little bird friend Lellie. I’m very grateful for how I can add my own goals (like “do duolingo”) and I can separate big tasks into “goal chunks”… so I added a “sort laundry” additionally to the “do laundry” task..) so if I don’t feel able to do the whole task of laundry in one day.. I can still feel like I accomplished something.. and with this app, I’ve found that breaking down the things I struggle with, often makes them feel more achievable and I get to reward myself for each goal I achieve rather than each whole task that I’ve done.. has been very helpful and made things feel less overwhelming x thank you for making this app x

So far, life changing!

author: Your Girl Emi

title: Outstanding
body:
This app has been extremely well researched and designed to support anyone in a journey to better self care and compassion. The default daily goals recognise that for some people, at some times, and maybe especially at a time they are seeking help, need low hurdles to reach rewards. Did you step outside your house today? Did you make your bed? Did you talk to anyone? These goals are compassionate and non judgemental and start the user on a gentle path to using Finch. How much you want to challenge yourself is up to you. Your baby finch will go on an adventure as soon as it has enough energy, and it gains energy by you completing your own goals…but not too many! So making your bed, drinking water and feeding your cat should get it under way. There are small rewards along the way, affirmations and support. If you indicate you are feeling low, the app will check in with you after a few hours and offer the resources in the first aid kit… breathing exercises, grounding exercises, journaling and guided meditations. All these features are free. A paid version will give you more options - for example allowing you to set times for certain goals or providing a wide range of journaling prompts. However, the free version has all the essentials for aiding someone with self care and mental health support. In addition, there is a “guardian” programme in which people can donate towards sponsoring a month of full membership for those who cannot afford it. If you wish, you can enter into a monthly raffle to receive a free membership for a month. And once you have set up specific goals and journal prompts with a paid membership (or donated one) returning to a free membership does not delete these settings. 
Overall this app is an act of compassion and an example of what a business model can look like if the developers genuinely have their customers wellbeing and health at the core of their mission.

title: A genius little app
body:
I have ADHD and am recovering from a pretty traumatic medical experience, so I’m struggling with brain fog and anxiety. This app was suggested to me by a friend and initially I wasn’t sure a cute bird going on adventures could help a grown man, but this app has genuinely changed my life.

My to-do list is visual and I get rewarded for completing them- from things as trivial as “going for a walk” to “take my medication” it has helped me reframe an overwhelming day.

Its breathing guides, reflections, exercises and guided journeys through anxious thoughts have all been genuinely helpful. 

It’s replaced my doom-scrolling of social media and I’m always interested to see what my little chap will have discovered on his adventure.

Like a tamagotchi, but the creature you’re taking care of is yourself.

I did not expect this app to be so detailed, so involved and so healing. 
Not only is it well polished, it has so much thought into it. For instance when you journal it picks up key words of positivity that you write and highlights them in bright colours. 

The entire premise of the app is fantastic. It’s cute- like insanely cute and yet clearly must have teams that understand the psychology of being in a state of wanting to develop one’s self care habits.

I cannot praise this enough- please give it a try if adulting overwhelms you. It is defo worth the download

title: One bit of feedback
body:
I’m new to the app, 5 days in so I’m not comfortable with giving it the 5 star treatment just yet, as I don’t want to incorrectly inform the masses. But all that to say, I love it so far! 

But I have one piece of feedback that I feel like would change the experience for me personally and perhaps others. I’ve noticed that finch is really big on mental health, even providing options to app goals for “tough days”. My suggestion is that there is another option under the custom goal setting that lets you set preemptive goals for “tough days” that are activated when you go onto the app and rate your mood, a sad face emoji would activate the tough day goals your have set just as the “first aid” pop up is activated when you rate your mood low anyway. 

It’s an incredibly small bit of feedback, and the only bit I have, so far, but I feel like it would make a huge difference and fit with the ethos of the app (or at least how I have interpreted it in my very small time on it).

title: The best app ever
body:
I never usually review things like this but I had to make the effort because I rarely come across such a well made app that has genuinely helped me feel better. 
The creators have thought of everything and I’ve never paid for the premium version of an app as quick in my life! It’s the perfect balance of being a fun game, an absolutely adorable pet (whom I’ve become irrationally attached to) and a self care tool.

I always remember to do my tasks because I love the moments with my little finch and the cute little messages they send you throughout the day is the most adorable thing ever!

It’s also really great that there’s everything in one app. I had a different app for breath work a different one for stretching and yoga exercises, a different one for meditation, a different one for organising myself with goals for the day and the list goes on. With this it’s literally all here and I get to use the points to buy the cutest little outfits.

Seeing my friends send me good vibes and encouragement randomly throughout the day reminds me that I’m on their mind and that I’m loved and I love how you can reflect on every part of it in a personal journal type of way.

Incredible thinking and thank you, it’s helped me feel so much better.

title: invaluable to my self-love journey
body:
What an incredible resource!

 This app has helped me to build routines around hygiene, eating, socialising, and mental health! I've told my friends and family about it and shared it during my group therapy session - I just want as many people to know about it as possible...

 I think this is a completely unique and well-planned app that can (and probably has) genuinely make a huge difference in someone's life!

 I've never been able to keep a bedtime routine but now I have one that I love and that keeps me healthy. My eating habits have also improved (something difficult as I am recovering from anorexia) and generally I have a much more motivated view on life in general!

 My favourite habit that was formed through this app is my self-compassion check. Every afternoon, I think about a recent situation where I was critical of myself and write down what my thoughts were (eg. I am so stupid for saying that). Then I picture someone I care about and think if they came to me with those words coming from their mouth, what would I say? (usually: 'Don't be so cruel to yourself, you did your best!') It is seriously helping me be more forgiving of myself in everyday life and I know this will help me grow.

 On top of all of this the design is ADORABLE and so engaging! When I lack the motivation to complete my goals for myself, sometimes looking at the clothes shop convinces me to wash my face so that my lil bird can have a cute hat! How clever manipulating the human mind like this haha

In all, I can't wait to see where I and little Sweetcheek will go and how we will grow during our time together. I hope to stuck around for a long time.

To anyone and everyone who worked on this app: Thank you, immensely.
