title: Too gamified and lost the mental health aspect
body:
I used to really love Finch, so much so that I paid for Plus membership. So I’m really sad to say that I absolutely hate the direction the app is heading in, and I will be letting my membership expire and because I can’t see myself using the app anymore using forward.

Previously when you opened the app, it would suggest tasks or activities based on the time of day and the mood you logged. All of these are now gone, and the mental health aspect of the game has been shoved off to the side where it’s way more complicated to access it. Now the app is just a to do list with bells on, with no care for the mental health aspect.

I should have seen it coming with the themed monthly events, but now there are “quests” to complete, and it’s become more about collecting rainbow stones and collecting objects and outfits. It’s only a matter of time before these become in game currency you pay for with real money. 

I didn’t download Finch for a fancy to-do list, I certainly didn’t download it as a game. I downloaded and PAID for it to help my mental health, an aspect that’s now complicated to access and made more convoluted with every update. 

I don’t care about the layout changing, I care that the function of the app is changing.

If I hadn’t invested money and time into this app I’d remove it as, I’ll be honest, like many other users who share the same feelings. It is not the same and is becoming more and more frustrating and disappointing. I want to do things simply, not have to spend extra time trying to find stuff and do stuff to set my bird off on his daily adventure.

Oh and you also desperately need to add more countries to get my bird to visit too as I’ve been stuck in Iceland for months and completed all the others as well.

Used to be 10/10, now more a 3.5/10

title: Changed my life
body:
I’ve now had this app for over a year and use it every day. I’ve tried a ton of them and they’re either overcomplicated, not engaging, put pressure on you or tell you off/passive aggressively make you feel bad for not doing a task. They also are often overwhelming with challenges and an ‘all at once’ attitude which is completely unsustainable for tasks especially if even brushing your teeth can be a struggle some days. 

Finch is the opposite. It’s cute, inviting, you have a sweet wholesome little bird buddy who keeps you accountable but is actually there to care for you, grow with you and for you to be able to nurture back. You can also connect with friends and their birds and send them hugs, thoughts, reminders to drink water etc which I love too. There’s a gameified element where if you complete a certain amount of tasks in a day it boosts your birds energy and they get to go on adventures to different places and tell you fun facts about where they’ve been. It’s sweet, it’s wholesome, there’s no pressure to put more than one task on there if that’s all you want or can manage. It reminds me of certain daily tasks which is really helpful but I don’t get told off if I don’t complete them all. 
They also have a scheme where you can pay to provide people who don’t have the financial means to pay for the app (I think it’s just ads you get if you have the free version) to have access to it. The paid version is also only a couple of pounds so it’s super accessible to those who can pay and similar to something like Duolingo it’s an app that it’s constantly being developed and you can see that thought and care is put into it. 

I’d give 6 stars if I could. Thank you for providing me and so many others a simple, sweet and thoughtful solution to self care and everyday tasks. 🐣💛

title: So helpful- highly recommend
body:
I’m a young (probably autistic) teenage girl who has many struggles with my mental health, but this app has helped me so much.
It is such a fun way to keep track of your habits and structure your day. It’s also obviously great for self-care, which is technically its main purpose, but I love how versatile it is, no matter what your goal is, Finch can help.

I love seeing my little pet grow every day, being able to decorate her house, and talking to her to see what she’s learnt at the end of her adventures (she’s currently exploring Paris!).

I really struggle with never having motivation but Finch has helped so much because if I can muster up just a tiny bit to go on the app, it’ll help me get through my tasks and help me feel better. It also has a morning motivation tracker, which I find really interesting to look at in the summary of every week (this also includes other interesting information such as what has “lifted you up” and had a negative impact on your week).

One really great thing is how it tracks all of your “tags”. Basically, whenever you log something on the app, it takes out key bits of information and turns them into “tags”. You can then view these tags individually and see if they overall affect you positively or negatively, and the things they are usually associated with when they give this affect.

There are also different quizzes on there for many different things. These are good for if you are wondering if you may have a condition (eg: anxiety, depression) but you want to be more sure before going to see someone. They ask you general questions and give you a summary at the end, but are still very clear that it is not a diagnostic tool, although I do believe self-diagnosis is almost always valid, it is good that they specify this.

There are so many other self-care tools on there too, but it would take me far too long to mention them all, a few are: breathing exercises, soundscapes, regular exercise guides and reflections.

It is sometimes a tiny bit irritating that quite a lot of options you have to pay for, but I completely understand that there is no better way to do it, as making an app is not free. I don’t think I’ve seen any other app handle having a subscription as well as this one though: the app is still fully functional without the subscription, it’s just some fun little bits you miss out on, there is the option to sponsor, and everyone who does becomes a “guardian” and is given a special mention on their kind of hall of fame type thing, and they do have a raffle kind of every month (I think) for those who really can’t afford it.

Overall, this app is perfect for anyone and everyone, whether you really struggle with mental health or simply want to keep up with some regular or self-care habits. Thank you so much to the people who made this, you are true superheroes <3

title: Made me realise I wasn’t alone
body:
I downloaded finch when I was in a rough time of my life, I didn’t have many friends or people who I thought cared about me and it was tough. I got this app to get me back on my feet and motivate me to do simple tasks like brush my teeth. The more tasks you do, the sooner your bird will come back from its adventure and level up which is really motivating (since you can unlock more colours for your bird and watch it grow and gain personality based on your options that you choose after the adventure). Anyways, I noticed there was a membership option after a week. Having the membership is completely optional and doesn’t affect the performance of the app, only really unlocking some bonus things such as soundscapes or fancy sunglasses for your bird and better rewards from the monthly pass. I then discovered there was a way you could put your name in a ‘guardian’ pot and have a chance to receive a free membership from a ‘guardian’ who is a kind person who pays out of their own pocket to gift someone else a membership. I decided to put my username in since I work a pretty bad retail job and don’t earn enough money to afford a membership not thinking anything of it. The new month rolls by and I get a notification saying that a guardian sponsored me, and you know at that moment I genuinely didn’t feel as alone as I did before, because some random person who I don’t even know was generous and thoughtful enough to gift someone else a little membership in a self care app. I realised at that point on people do care and I just need to focus on healing. I am essentially back on my feet because of this app.

Another note: after my guardian membership ran out, I had a notification asking if I wanted to support the devs and buy a membership (with an amazing discount) however this was during/close to Christmas and I literally only had £10 in my bank account (if I had more I 100% would’ve gone with the deal it was amazing), so I hastily clicked with the option to continue for free, but then the app gave me a membership anyways!! And that the devs just hope that I’d return the good deed in the future. Like what?!! What type of app cares so much about their player base that it just gives away free memberships?!!!! Honestly unbelievably generous and caring devs that run and make this app. When I next get paid I’m going to buy my own membership and try and support this app however I can because it’s so great. 

10/10

title: If you’re looking for an app to get yourself back, this is it.
body: I was diagnosed with EUPD in 2018 and have struggled with elements of the disorder, my sense of self and routine were parts that I found help on with this app. This app has healed so much in me it’s kind of unbelievable. It’s the best app for mental health I’ve ever used. I got gifted a premium membership from a guardian as I was struggling so much mentally I wasn’t working and didn’t have any income. It helped me form routines and really connect with myself again. I’m now completely sober, medicated, stable and HAPPY. You’re able to choose outfits for your little finch bird and watch them grow each day, it really starts to feel like an extension of yourself. You do quizzes to check in on yourself regularly, answer questions and notes to yourself and it #’s key words and names and forms reports each month on correlations you might not notice yourself. You get to choose what you want to add to your daily routines, from brushing your teeth to calling your mum. With each thing you do you feel a genuine sense of accomplishment. You can even add people and send them encouragement or just a little dance to keep them going too. There’s more too, like things you can listen to to calm down, meditation and a first aid section for when you’re in crisis that will help you through things like a panic attack. I’m not saying this app will fix any and all mental health issues, but from my personal experience it’s helped me a lot. And it’s absolutely worth a try if you’re struggling. Thank you Finch!

title: Thank you
body: This is one of my top apps, it’s so wonderful and I highly recommend paying the annual subscription. It is very versatile and customisable so you can get it to work for your wellbeing and benefit. For example I’m someone who loves lists and the goals you can set on here daily or weekly ect, are completely customisable and you can link them to certain journeys like health or creativity and helps you see how doing the little things each day build up. If someone is more into journaling then there’s plenty of space to write your thoughts. There’s the element of kindness between members and an option to add people who aren’t members onto a family tree so you can see you support network. Not forgetting there breathing exercises, yoga and stretch routines you can do with the help of the app. There’s so much more I could say because there’s little treasures everywhere in this app and it’s been a real source of comfort and reliability for me during some very dark periods of my life.

title: Unethical High-Pressure Sale Tactics
body:
Regardless of how good the app really is, I have decided not to go forward with it after the first five minutes because shortly after hatching the pet, giving it a name, and other things that would naturally attach the pet to me, the app threw a “one-time limited offer for plus” in my face. 

It was an offer for a 7 day free trial followed by a 43% discount for a yearly subscription (the discounted rate is £40 which is still a lot of money!)- and the offer stated it would be gone if I clicked off the screen. This is a really egregious and unethical method of monetization which is designed to pressure people into making a snap decision to pay in. I would be irritated seeing this from any app, much less one targeted towards vulnerable people. 

If you are a developer of this app, please know that I understand you need to pay for your staff, development costs, etc. I was prepared to pay a reasonable amount for a subscription if I enjoyed the app on its free tier but this “one-time offer” has put me off just on principle.

title: ⭐️ Finch FULL REVIEW ⭐️
body:
👋 Hello! Here is my detailed review on the Finch app!

ℹ️ My Opinion: In my opinion, Finch is the BEST self care app out there! I have tried a lot of them, and this one is the only app that is not money hungry, fun and makes me super happy!

👶 Age Rating: Any Age!

I think that this game is for everyone! I made my nana get it, my mum, my dad my sister, and my friends! And they all love it! I really like being able to take care and dress up my bird! And can’t wait to see what kind of adventure he would have gone up! Anybody would love it!

💰 Costs: Free or Subscription.

The subscription in Finch is called Finch Plus, it’s and very accessible to everyone! It’s cheap, and even if you can’t afford it, you can enter the raffle and somebody can sponsor you. Normally, you win the raffle within 1 to 3 times of trying. I got it on my first try! And after your sponsor ends, they give you the option to a cheaper finch plus subscription or if you can’t afford it, you get it for free. I have not seen any other app do this, and I really love finch for it! Please don’t change it! :)

🟢 Pros: You get to name, decorate and your bird will go on adventures and find new things every day. E.G Today, my bird discovered a juice carton. And I had to explain it to him when he had a question about it. And he will either like it or not! Finch also has quizzes about Stress, anxiety and depression and you can do lots of different breathing exercises and reflections and goals for the day! My bird feels like a friend to me who is real it’s that good!

🔴 Cons: I have had this app for 677 days and I honestly can’t think of anything bad about it! It’s just perfect!

❓Conclusion: I really think you should download finch and give it a go! Even if you don’t have finch plus, it still has everything you need! :)

😄I hope this review has helped :)

title: just wonderful.
body:
i have never felt compelled to write a review for an app before, but after using finch for the last couple months i can say that i am MORE than satisfied. the team have created a beautiful space, filled with community, love, and hope. i have adhd and i am autistic. i have always struggled in the past to take care of myself, attempting to-do lists and productivity apps, and putting myself down when i found things hard. 

with a bit of effort from my end, and encouragement from a little bird, i have made an effort to log in every day, take care of myself when i can, reflect on my life and my relationships and develop an even healthier, kinder relationship with myself. 
the end goal is not productivity, not to tick off everything on your list every single day. it’s to do what you can, when you can. it’s to survive the day. to make an effort to appreciate the moments in your life whenever you can.

i didn’t have many expectations for the app when i first downloaded it, but every day i discover more about the app, about myself, and i feel more optimistic about my life and my future than i have ever been.

i know this isn’t all down to an app, it took effort from myself too. but to have a place to put my thoughts, to channel my energy into something positive and see what is fulfilling me, what may be dragging me down, to remind myself of reflections i’ve written and people that i love, altogether has really helped me in my journey.

i hope that other people can find this app and extend love towards themselves and towards other people.

sending finch hugs to anybody reading this, and i wish you the best.
(i also hope this made sense lol)

much love :)

title: amazing🤷‍♀️
body:
I’ve had this app for 30 days now and I think it’s helped me keep track of what I need to do and what I’m doing. It also helps me get stuff done an also helps me with getting stuff done and ready for the day. It’s really easy to use honestly, and it’s cute how the finch grows close every time to grow up. 

I like the way you can customise your finch later on while having it, you can decide the colours, the clothing and it’s really fun. You can also buy clothing for the finch in the shop. You can also decorate your finches room, the clothing aren’t free but you get diamonds for free everyday so you can save up or spend! I have over 9000 saved over the 30days I’ve been using this.

I’ve got finch plus, cause you can get things also for free like season offers. You get diamonds, clothing and stuff to decorate the room of your finches. You can also kind of get this when you don’t have finch plus, you get diamonds and I’m sure you could get some other things. I’ve forgot to be fair as I’ve had finch plus for a while.

I really recommend this so you realise how good you’re getting on and everything.

I also forgot to mention that you can create your own tasks and write how you felt about them.

title: Highly recommend! 💗
body:
This is an amazing app and one of my favourite apps I’ve come across. It is very good with selfcare, before I found this app I never wanted to do anything due to my depression but once I got the app it really helped me get back into my daily routine and selfcare again. I highly recommend getting Finch. It is such a perfect app for selfcare and it’s so helpful! It makes selfcare seem a lot easier and more fun to do. 

One thing I do wish for is that a text message box would be added so we can actually talk to people on the app because sometimes I want to write a paragraph to someone to say how much I love their birds outfit or just a kind message to say they’re doing well and have a little chat with them. If that was added I would give finch a 5 star rating. 

Overall the app is very good and I highly recommend getting.

title: Thank You
body:
I rarely leave reviews, but I’m so glad to have downloaded this app. I struggle with mental health and often get overwhelmed by the smallest everyday things, so being able to have my goals for the day right in front of me really helps.

My mood has improved in 2 days, which I honestly am amazed by. Sometimes I forget how much the littlest things matter. Oh, and I love the reflections feature! It really helps with getting my thoughts out, and find positives in ways I hadn’t really thought to do before. I really enjoy the words of encouragement that are sprinkled throughout this app, too.

I must admit, at first the idea of a self-care “pet” seemed a little silly to me, but I now realise that it simply adds that little bit of fun that some people need to start making a difference. Better yet, birds are my favourite animal, haha!

So, thank you, I am really enjoying this app. It has really been a useful tool to me so far.

title: I love Cabbage
body:
This app was a recommendation from a friend. I struggle to stick with anything (ADHD) so I expected to use it for a week and then forget about it like everything else. 
To my surprise, I’ve used it every day and have gotten my friends using it too. I love Cabbage (my little birdy baby), and I would anything for them.
It doesn’t feel overwhelming to use, and there are so many useful features. The tagging system is brilliant, and the clothing and furniture are super cute. I like the breathing exercises and stretches a lot!
I’d love to see gifting implemented in this app! I see things in the shop that I’d like to send to my friends, and I think it would be a great feature! It would also be cool to see our friend’s houses!

title: Amazing!!!
body: I love this app so much, it’s helped me a lot with being more organised, clean, and happy in general. Everyday I fill in the goals I’ve completed and if there’s any I haven’t done, i go through and do them one by one. These tasks include of: Put away one thing that’s not in its place, make your bed, brush your hair, complete a breathing exercise, step outside for 1 minute, and so much more. I have the finch widget on my home screen which allows you to check up on your Birb. Every day, Muffin (the name of my Birb) goes on an 8 hour long adventure. You can shorten the time they are away for by completing your goals, doing breathing exercises, yoga, reflect on your day etc. As you meet your goals daily your Birb will grow. Mine is currently 1.5cm tall and is almost a toddler. I recommend this app if you are struggling with mental health, or even just want to be more organised and healthy. :)

title: The First Self Care App that’s actually Worked for me!
body:
If I have any recommendations, this app would DEFINITELY be on the list! Get your friends on this app too! Getting gifts and messages in the morning is super motivating!
I’ve only been on this app for about a week and I’ve gone from rolling out of bed to check my phone a couple times and then trying to sneak in 5, 10, 15 extra minutes of sleep, to stretching before I go to bed, and having a full routine in the morning that includes washing my face, moisturising and brushing my teeth, which I honestly never used to do. As a teenager I think that stuff’s actually pretty damn important too. And getting motivating little notifications from my Finch saying stuff like “I look up to you Tuesday!” Is super cool too!
The app’s super cute and the game-like aspect I think is one of the most motivating aspects to keep up all the good work! And I haven’t even *started* with all the features on this thing, honestly, just download it and give it a go yourself!

title: Review of an amazing app ❤️
body:
I’ve had Finch for a while now. My friend recommended it to me and I’m honestly so glad that she did. My birb and the Finch community have helped me so much, and the app itself is easy to use. I love watching my birb grow, and chatting to her after her adventures. The best part is that you take care of your birb by taking care of yourself, and this has really made self-care a bigger part of my life now. This is such a creative and interesting way to put self-care first to those who would never have done it before. Five out of five stars, would definitely recommend to anyone thinking of getting the app! ❤️

I’d also like to say a quick thanks to the developers too. You’ve helped me through some tough days. Keep doing what you’re doing! 🌈🫶🏻

title: Brilliantly constructed App!
body:
I suffer for depression and have for a lot of years. Medication helps but I didn’t want to be reliant on it. I have tried a few apps for mindfulness but couldn’t really engage with them and quickly gave up. 

This app gets you interested by looking after a widget finch. Each interaction stimulates and grows the finch and thus helps you. You energise your finch by doing mindfulness things in the morning and while you work your finch is off ‘travelling’ for 6 hours so if you don’t have time to interact during to day, don’t worry. The finch looks after it’s self! 

The app is packed full of mindfulness things and activities to help you cope with daily life. I particularly like the thought dump and rant zone notes, and the extensive selection of soundscapes that can run anything from 10mins to 8 hours. I use the breathing techniques if particularly stressed at work. 

I have been using the app since January and my finch has now grown to adult size. I actually enjoy interacting with her and I like the like pop up notifications that I get from the app throughout the day. 

I have felt less depressed as I have used the app and I think that it is well worth the money for the yearly subscription! 

Overall a very good app to get you to do mindfulness on a daily basis!

title: Recommended, my daughter loves!
body: My daughter suffers from anxiety and through her little birdie who she name Belinda spaghetti, she has been able to analyse her own actions and help herself. One time, Belinda spaghetti finds a cherry on a walk and doesn’t like it. My daughter used this to know that it’s ok when you put effort into things and they end up a different way, still be proud of yourself for getting it done. This has helped so much with school work and exam season. I highly recommend!! Tomorrow we’re going on a walk and buying some cherries on the way back, this way we can talk about how to adapt our lifestyles to fit into working for her!

title: Amazing!
body: I love this app and use it daily. I love all the different types of goals you can set yourself (there is something there for literally everyone). I especially love the ‘those days’ ones like ‘just be’ and ‘literally survive the day’. I love all the outfits and adorable accessories you can get for your finch and your not that restricted if you don’t have Finch Plus. Another thing I love about this app is it recognises not everyone can afford to pay for Finch Plus so it often gives you discounts or little messages saying they appreciate everyone on the app. I also love the raffle done every month. I was lucky enough to win and got a Guardian Angel who pays for Finch Plus for me. There are no words to describe my gratefulness towards my Donor. Not to mention the finch tree that you can add friends and family to and send pick up messages to each other. All in all I love this app so much and hope everyone else doesn’t too.

title: Has become overly gamified
body:
I used to find this app good and useful, but the reduction in features accessible to free users and overt push towards having a subscription is somewhat harmful. I’ll be uninstalling this app and looking for an alternative.

For those unable to afford a subscription the only option is to enter a raffl. There is no pay once option. Someone’s mental health should not be tied to a game of chance.

Additionally, preying on those susceptible to Fear Of Missing Out by adding a season pass and locking items behind the aforementioned subscription seems exceptionally dubious for an app whose intent is to help someone with their mental health.

title: Ideas
body:
Right, so I love this app and it’s really good at making me care for myself because I want to energise my bird, however I have a few suggestions that could make the game even better:
1. Make it so you can gift items to your friends on the app. I think this would be so cool especially if you are waiting for a specific item do ages and if it finally came up on a friends account you could have it.
2. If I energise my bird for the scheduled wake up time, I’ll still get a notification that she’s just woken up at that time. This is pretty weird as I already know that she’s awake and it doesn’t make much sense to tell me she’s just woken up later.
3. I love the events however if you’re not a plus user most of what you get is furniture. I understand that there has to be a bit of a difference between the two modes, however it would be nice to get less than just hundreds of doors and carpets.

title: Recent updates are demotivating
body:
Edit: I used to love this app and it truly got me through some difficult times but the recent updates are very demotivating. The push for users to pay for Finch Plus (approx £33) has simply created a sense of missing out, and elitism for those us who can’t afford it. I completely understand the devs need and deserve to be paid, but I don’t enjoy using the app now that I can’t get the cool items. Currently, the starry collection is only available in blue if you pay for it and missing out on this, is disappointing enough for me to avoid opening Finch altogether. As a loyal user, please please find a different way for Finch plus to work. My favourite self-care app has become a capitalism simulator.

(Original review) :
I never leave reviews but I truly love this app. It’s beautifully designed and intuitive to use. It’s helps me shift my mood from a horrible place to an okay one in times of need. You can tell the people who developed it actually care about your mental health rather than just trying to make money because the prompts and suggested tasks are so gentle yet effective. For example one suggested goal is ‘brush your teeth’ which might seem silly to some people but it’s actually achievable if you’re somebody struggling with your mental health. The little bird character is so cute and says some funny things but not in such a way that I cringe at myself for using the app. I feel like this app was designed with a lot of empathy. I love how much journaling and self-reflection it encourages in an unintimidating way. I end up writing so much and learning to self-sooth without even realising it. Yet, I don’t feel dependent on the app because it teaches you that you can care for yourself. I really love it!! title: Amazing
body:
This app is very helpful - helping to motivate me to get my daily chores done - looks good - with a range of collectible furniture and outfits for me to save points for. I’ve only been using it for a week now but I hope to keep at it. I also like all the self reflection tasks you can do!

 Improvements: 
-It can be a little difficult to make new tasks sometimes as for some reason they don’t show up sometimes or let you set the correct date but it’s been working most of the time. 
-setting and looking at all your tasks is also a little unintuitive. I wish that it was separated into daily, weekly, set dates. One so its easier to look through the ones you’ve already set instead of it being a massive list. Two because there doesn’t seem to be a way to say you need to do something once a week without setting a set day for it. But sometimes I can’t do that and just wanna get it done by the end of the week.
 -I would love a to-do section to set tasks that don’t have to be done on a set day but instead for a certain deadline or even just whenever. Mostly to remind me of things I want to do, but have it in the same app as my daily tasks cause at the minute I’m using multiple.

title: The new interface is horrible for my AuDHD brain
body:
I loved this app and found it incredibly useful (bar the bugs that I reported months ago which still persist because "we're only a small team!"), but sadly the recent updates to the journey system have made it really frustrating and overloading for me use. 

 I'm Autistic with ADHD and really appreciated the calm, organised layout that the app previously used for the journey system as it was clear to navigate and required zero 'menu diving'; the new one is just an extremely colourful, cramped, busy list with journeys stacked on top of each other and incredibly 'loud' and overwhelming. 

It would be great to have an option to revert back to the old design for those of us who are overloaded by this new one (and it would be even greater to get those persistent bugs I've reported fixed too). I honestly wish I could transfer my plus membership to someone who's going to use the app, because in its new format it just isn't usable for me at all, and believe me, I've tried.

title: Please please get this app!
body: I don’t usually write reviews for apps but this app really made me feel like I have to. If this review persuades you then I feel like I have helped an extra person in society. So not to be tmi but I struggle with my mental health quite a bit, I found keeping basic tasks in my head, journaling and just getting out of bed very difficult. This app roles it all in to one! I have suggested all my friends to get the app and they are all my tree pals! We send eachother support and reminders to drink water, stretch etc. This app also measures what reflections you put and helps you understand what might be wrong and what words you use commonly with names of places and even people. For example you may have shown 17 reflections that week with work and anxiety. It can help you understand where you might need to improve your life to better your mental health. It also gives you goals like drink water, make bed, brush teeth and those goals can be altered to ‘help improve you and so and so’s relationship’. Oh and did I even mention?! Every thing you do in the app, helps energise a baby bird that grows with you through your mindful journey! And you can have conversations with and get close to!!! Personally for me I’m a student and I can’t afford the premium version ( not because of the price I just don’t have enough money) but I find the free version to be enough for me for now, but if you can afford to, I highly suggest to get the premium version, you get to adapt your goals a little better and have better newsletters and insights. What really rocked the boat for me and made it amazing compared to other apps was that some goals include activities like mindful breathing, or listening to relaxing rain noises.. I’m also pretty sure there are INSTRUCTIONAL YES INSTRUCTIONAL step by step video stretching sessions!! How cool is that?! For a minute or so! So so cool. Basically if you struggle with your mental health, I suggest you get the app and try it out, what’s there to lose? You spend a day with your own baby bird and you don’t like the app? Fair enough. But if you do like it… then you start your mental health journey with a little bird that grows with you!!! Thank you Finch team for creating an ace app :)))))

title: Thank you for helping me put me first - and my finch, Mochi.
body: I downloaded finch a couple of days ago when I was looking for an anxiety help app that I haven’t tried before, because I was on the verge of tears at work because my anxiety was so bad. No other app has helped, I end up using it for one day then deleting it because I didn’t actually feel encouraged to use it or like it has a better purpose. My little finch Mochi, has encouraged me to take care of myself and put my self care first, because you take care of your finch by taking care of you. My anxiety has improved so much and I get excited to complete tasks, to watch my finch grow and see what she discovers when she’s on her adventures. Its given my self care a purpose. I’ve never been so encouraged to take care of myself before, I feel this sense of care over Mochi and ultimately, I’m caring for myself. Not only that, the app has so many different activities that there is so much to discover that can help you that you’ve never thought of before. I love everything about the app, I’m so excited to see how it can develop, it’s already so great. One thing I would suggest, is I would love to play games with Mochi, as games tend to distract me when my anxiety is bad, it would be a cool feature if you can actually do things with your finch as such. I love this app so much, thank you for helping me, it’s such an innovative, creative idea! ❤️🥺

title: LOVE IT
body:
Right, so this is my second review of this incredible app, I’m here again simply because I feel that I didn’t go into enough detail last time. 

Where can I start? I have had finch for about 9 months now and my birb, Cheddar has helped me see the positive side in everything. The fact that this app is free to download is awesome because it is 100% worth downloading. 

Now, I recently purchased premium on finch because I was loving spending time on there every day and I wanted to enhance that and premium is also 100% worth it. With premium you get more quizzes, activities, mail, more access to the shop, and additional seasonal premium outfits.

On finch, you obviously start of with your very own finchie pet. You get to name it and everything!! The more you play, the older your pet gets. You can also design a room for your pet to spend time in whilst you complete activities. 

At the start of each day, my birb greets me and tells me a quote for the day. He either asks ‘How motivated are you for today?’, ‘How is your day going so far?’ Or ‘How satisfied are you with today?’ Depending on the time. You will then begin your activities. For each positive activity, you get a certain amount of rainbow stones, once you get 30, your finch goes on a days adventure. If you want them back faster, you will complete more activities. 

And then on top of that, you can also spend time in the finch shop to buy accessories for your pet.

Overall I LOVE finch. It gets me through hard times and even when I’m happy, it helps me see the positive in everything!! Thank you finch!!! 

-tilly 07/11/2022 💜

I love seeing the different shades of green and red on the different days and seeing when I was feeling happier and being able to see what I did that day from my reflections. title: Loving This App
body:
I have a potential ADHD style brain and can struggle with my well-being despite being highly functional everywhere else. Someone recommended this app to me. I love having everything in one place such as soundscapes, stretches, personal daily goals, space to reflect etc. and I’m sure I’ve only used a fraction of what’s available. Interacting with my fondly named ‘Wooble’ actually keeps it interactive for me, which suits my brain. If I just had an app to write my goals in I would soon stop using it. 

A massive highlight for me has been the soundscapes - I didn’t appreciate how they would affect my mood and help me focus. I love them. Also, I stop and reflect now on a regular basis and I really value that.

Would highly recommend this app to anyone with a brain like mine!

title: Life Changing
body:
Finch is the best self-care app out there. Especially for people suffering with mental health related problems and ADHD etc. I suffer with depression, anxiety, PTSD, emetephobia and likely ADHD (it’s a long diagnosis progress). Routines have never been achievable, in any form; reflections, building healthy habits etc. Finch ENSURES I check in with my brain daily. Evaluate my feelings, keep track of what is making me happy and sad, build healthy habits etc. Since downloading the app I have started going to the gym consistently, I’m eating healthier and keeping track of my mood. All because of a cute little bird. Because of my mental health problems, I haven’t cared much for my own happiness. However, a little bird? Who needs me? He has forced me to care for myself so I can care for him. I don’t think he has ever missed a daily adventure as a result of me completing my tasks, even if it isn’t all of them.  

And to whoever made this app, you genuinely have helped to change my life. I whole heartedly thank you for that. I told myself if I keep up with Finch daily for 6 months I will buy myself the full version (if I can afford it). But that’s the beauty of it, the free version is still good enough. Yet there are aspects of the app I wish I could use because if the free version is great what will the full version help me achieve?

Thankyou, whole heartedly. 
Emmie & Yoshi (my finch)

title: Awesome and adorable
body:
I never normally write reviews but I have to make my thoughts known; I think it is fantastic. The concept of the app a great way to make you realise that anything can be an achievement to you no matter how small, and reflecting on the positives every day has really lifted my mood, even on days that I feel my worst. It’s also got opportunities for writing down worries or sleep problems etc which there’s not much opportunity to document in every day life, so you feel like you’ve got something off your chest. I love the little things about the bird too - naming it, looking after it and it shows you its little personality traits which is adorable. There’s also quizzes and little meditations which I’ve always found helpful. 

I have struggled with anxiety and a chronic illness for years and the healthcare in my country is terrible so it’s difficult to get treatments for mental health, obviously it’s not a cure or therapy or anything but this app does make me feel a bit brighter.

body:
Finch is an amazing self care app and it 100% helps! I definitely recommend to ALL ages!
Is it free? Most parts are free including quizzes, daily goals, your finch bird and much more but you can buy a subscription for £2.38 a month which unlocks a few more quizzes and some extra goals!
Does it help with anger/depression? Yes! There are multiple rant zones that you can just write how you feel without anybody finding out what you wrote! There are also positive zones that you can go back and read to remind you about happy things!
Can you play with friends? Yes you can! All you need to do is add them to your tree town and you can send positive vibes every day to each other!
I hope this helped you and once again I really recommend you download Finch!

title: I am terrible at keeping up with these apps. This is the only one I’ve ever stuck to.
body:
TL;DR Try it, you won’t lose any sleep if you don’t like it, but if it fits well with you (like me) then it’s a life saver! 
 
Creating a cute animal is only the beginning. This app has little ACHIEVABLE goals for you to pick from daily, it allows you to create a todo list, is has its little bits of humor. I’m hooked, genuinely. I celebrated 100 active days on the app a few days back. 

This is honestly the only mental health app I’ve ever stuck to. My favourite feature (apart from an interactive to do list) is deffo a weekly review. It shows what’s been getting you down, and what’s made you happy.

 I have actually recommended this to other depresso friends, and they are also actively using it. The option to link up is there, but I’ve opted not to use it. 

 All in all, I really truly do recommend this app. If you don’t like it you can always delete it.

author: Mrs.Grint <3

title: Honestly, I love it.
body:
I never really believed in using little apps for improving my mental state, but then I saw an Instagram add for this adorable little bird that gets to grow with you and I just had to try it out. I opened the app and created my baby chick; Hugo.  

Usually I never return to these apps, I try them out for a day and then delete the app a few days later because I forget they even existed. But every morning I wake up and the first thing I do is check in on Hugo, I write away and complete my morning routine. I haven’t had the app for long, but it’s done so much for me. 

All throughout the day I receive these lovely messages from the app, and get handy reminders for things I wanted to complete throughout the day. There is a still a lot more room for improvement but I know that if I keep using Finch that gap will get smaller. Honestly, if you’re struggling to get yourself into a routine, or to push yourself outside of your comfort zone then this is the app to get. I love opening the app and getting rate my current emotion, it makes me sit and think about just how much really happens in a day.

I never leave reviews, but this one had to be written. Thank you, Finch Team. <3

title: A great idea well made
body: I’m 33 and I wondered if I might find this a bit childish. I like to think of myself as competent and rational, but the truth is my self care has been lacking recently. I enjoy playing games on my phone so I figured that this might help me make some progress and so far it seems to be working. It’s a simple concept- set your intentions, and get rewarded for them. The little characters are cute and friendly, and never tell you off or complain. The built-in targets are reasonable (get out of bed, leave the house etc) and you can also add your own. If you’re struggling with your mental health this is a great way of building some better habits.

title: Adorable
body:
Warning: I’m a writer so my review is long and looks like it’s been written by a bot but I promise it’s real 😂 

I’ve been playing Finch for a bit over 3 weeks now, and I LOVE IT. I’m not someone who usually follows through with things, I usually just forget or lose motivation, but that hasn’t happened with Finch! 

My Finch is called Moonleap - I love that you can name them and pick their pronouns! Moonleap has they/them pronouns. 

This app has encouraged me to participate in morning stretches, light exercises, cleaning my room, and just generally a lot of self-care.

I’ve only ever missed one or two adventure days, I always try and remember to make room for Moonleap, which is basically like making room for myself to participate is self-care exercises.

I love that you can dress them, and that you can influence their personality SO MUCH!

Anyway, all I’m trying to say, is that you should definitely download Finch, even if you don’t feel like you’ll follow through. Thank you for taking the time to read. :)

title: self care bird makes me smile
body:
This app is amazing, and the only app my ADHD brain has managed to continue using for more than a few months so I was able to subscribe to their premium model.

I struggle with doing self care regularly and this app has provided me with a gamified way to make my self care much more consistent. I absolutely love how non-judgemental and open the goals can be (from keeping personal health goals all the way to keeping charitable goals) and the new Journeys feature makes it so fun to try to improve an area of your life. 

I love how the easiest way to get energy is through reflections because it almost forces you to engage in mindfulness thinking, which I often struggle with. All because my pet bird HAS to go on her walk today or I’ll feel bad!

I also love how you can make a little town full of your friends, whether they have the app or not. I enjoyed interacting with my friends birds on the app, where they can visit your bird and then go on adventures together. Even if they stopped using it, I still get visits from the Finch Team and I think that’s really sweet!! (Shout out to Toot Toot and Alex, what a name for a bird!)

I also love how often the app is updated for the better. I’ve had this app for half a year now and it has updated very regularly to be even better than I could have thought, the UI is easy to understand and I really enjoy all the new costumes for my little bird to enjoy.

I hope the developers are proud of their creation because they’ve done so well!

title: Incredible App, Beautiful Community & Caring developers
body:
Like many people who have reviewed this app, I always only use self care apps for a few days - maybe even a week before forgetting, giving up or just not really finding it suitable for me.
Finch is completely different. I’m over 40 days in and I can’t foresee me stopping to pop in on the app several times a day. Even on my busiest or most stressful days, even popping on to look at Carjas adventures, check up on goals or flick through the shop can be enough to lift me up a little. Other days I find myself writing so much information in the sections and it gives me a huge sense of relief to get things written out, or replay a funny memory or answer some wonderfully odd questions. 
The community for Finch on Facebook is beautiful and the dev team actually listen and put action on user suggestions. This is an app that will continue to improve and continue to help thousands of people. 

This is a beautifully designed, easy to use app with few glitches. Recommended for all.

title: Really good app <3
body:
I love this app; all the features are useful, and I enjoy scrolling through all the stats and notes I’ve made throughout the day. It helps with self-care and the little penguin is adorable! I really love this app <3

There are a couple of things I think could be improved, though: 
1) when the app identifies words you use often — I’ve noticed it categorises words then puts a square of green or red on the mood calendar depending on whether it thinks you have positive or negative associations with that thing, but that part often seems quite random and I’ve ended up with several red squares on the calendar for things I really enjoy. 
2) the identifying words thing — I like the idea of this feature it just seems a little random to me and not as organised as I’d maybe like it to be. Some of the things from my reflections have been mis-categorised and it’s just a bit annoying. 
3) the exercises seem a little long — I’d suggest maybe 30 seconds on the left and 30 on the right? One minute just seems like quite a long time. 

Overall, I really enjoy using this app so far and it’s definitely helpful. Thank you!

title: Only self care app that has worked for me!
body:
This app is absolutely amazing. I have tried several self-care apps but haven’t stuck with any before I found Finch.
Finch has honestly changed my life and finally got me to engage with self-care. I struggle to find the motivation to do self-care tasks for myself, but seeing my finch grow and discover new things as I look after myself has been the motivation I need. I also love that Finch encourages me to set small, simple goals like brushing my teeth and literally getting through the day, and all the goals are equally weighted so I still feel the same sense of achievement.
I also have anxiety around breathing exercises which so many other apps rely on, so I like that I can just mute these on Finch.
The app and the animations and bright colours are also so cute and positive, and I love seeing what my finch discovers each day on their adventures. It’s helped me to see small new discoveries in my own life as ‘adventures’ too.
I really am so grateful for this app and would recommend it to anyone, especially if you find self-care tricky and you love cute things!

author: Cazmum

title: free features are great and RSD friendly
body:
the amount of features you can try for free is absolutely perfect, meaning the useful parts of the app are not locked behind a paywall. while there is still incentive to pay for a subscription, if i feel to do so i know it would be completely of my volition and not frustration and wishful thinking. this app just functions as it should i think its one of the best balances i've experienced. 

also as someone with ADHD i appreciate that this app focuses on awarding consistent behaviour as well as encouraging you to want to use the app and not just coercing you back in with time limits and manipulative notifications. i also love that there is little in the way of punishment or detriment for not maintaining consistent use, which is a must for me because i will aways inevitably drop off for a while but i can just continue on my path to introspection and mindfulness without feeling that my natural tendency to be inconsistent is in the way of my progress. i always feel welcomed back. positive reinforcement all the way! i feel seen :')

title: Actually helpful!
body:
I don’t usually write reviews but I felt compelled to write one for this app. I’ve been using it for 3 days now and been super helpful! I suffer with severe anxiety and a panic disorder. Day to day life can be quite emotionally taxing but using this app every so often throughout my day for breathing exercises, breaking down my thoughts into manageable bites with their reflective activities and using the soundscapes at night has honestly made me feel so much better. I love that there’s a choice of different breathing exercises depending on what you need but not only that they actually explain the breathing technique and why it works. There’s links all over the app to studies that all the information has been taken from which I really appreciate. Finally as an added bonus you have a cute little penguin buddy to support you on your journey! I’m so happy I found this app and I will absolutely be purchasing the full version once my free trial has expired. 
Thank you so much to the developers of this app, I can really feel how much love and effort has gone into creating this. Well done guys, you’ve nailed it.

title: Perfect self care app!
body:
I love this app, been playing for a week now and it’s brilliant. I’m the sort of person who does better with a little ‘pet’ to motivate me. I’ve used other self care pet apps and they work temporarily but then I max out the levels and I get bored, but this is a slower paced app with a huge range of exercises, with a slower progression with the pet. Will keep me invested for much longer! 

I love that you can refresh wording of prompts, I also love that you can ‘mute’ prompts that aren’t your thing. The goal setting the night before is the biggest win for me, along with the morning motivation check in and evening satisfaction check in. As somebody who generally has an overwhelming to do list, I love being able to section off the Self-Care side in this app so it doesn’t get overlooked. I manage to find time for 5 jumping jacks to earn rainbow stones with Finch whereas otherwise I’d just sit still! 

I love the pet customisations and conversations with the pet, choosing what you want to nurture in their personalities. 

Love everything! Well done Finch creators, you’re changing lives. Please keep developing this app, excited to see where it goes!

title: Unique app, really helpful but needs some improvements
body:
I’m not buying the full version just because there are some parts of the app that are lacking and need improvement. The main one is the stretching exercises. In my opinion each exercise should be 30 seconds long (right side 30secs then left side 30secs) not 1 minute for each side, it’s too long. It also isn’t helpful if you choose a 1 minute exercise because according to the app you can only do one side of your body in that minute. It would also be helpful if it was explained how to do the exercises. I do yoga and stretching so I’m familiar with some but people who don’t might not be. 

Another thing which I think would improve the app is being able to write your own goals on the goals section instead of having to choose from a list. 

Overall though, this app has really helped me with my journalling and evening reflections which is what I download it for. If those few things were improved the app would be perfect! And would be worth buying it

author: Shychick

title: Self care with a price
body:
I’ve found this app extremely helpful in keeping me motivated. I’ve been in and out of counselling and therapy for years and have always struggled to motivate myself to so things even if they’re ultimately helpful and i found Finch’s creative way of motivating the player very helpful.

However i do have a gripe on the micro transactions. They’re not terribly intrusive thankfully but i find it weird and a tad exploitative to have them so easily accessible and in your face at times when vulnerable people will be using the app. For example whilst my Finch was on a quest i wanted to shuffle the tasks i can do as the ones there didn’t suit but nope that feature is paywalled, as well as a few other features and quality of life things. I don’t think the devs intend to be predatory at all, and i respect their mission to keep mental health help free and the fact that bills have to be paid the lights need to be kept on etc, i just think there might be better ways to raise money then charging the player for features that could ultimately help their mental health? Especially with the target audience of the app undeniably being vulnerable people. Maybe try having the subscription just be optional for those who want to support the app like donations? Or keep the charges just to cosmetics for the finch instead of app features? Idk, just some food for thought.

If you’re not vulnerable to spending sprees, i say absolutely download this app! For whats free, it’s great and i definitely recommend it. But if you’re vulnerable for that sort of thing maybe give this one a pass. I hope everyone’s having a good day, stay safe!

title: Can’t Recommend This Enough
body:
I have never used a self-care app so great. I usually end up deleting such apps after 2 to 3 days because I lack the motivation to keep up with them, but I have had this for over a week and have no plans of ever getting rid of it. I really can’t recommend it enough.

The best parts are:
+ ‘Raising’ the pet isn’t taxing at all. It starts its journey in the morning and comes back after 6/7 hours to share what it found and learnt.
+ You can keep it as a widget(!!!) This really helped me because I often forget about apps if they’re hidden away in folders, but seeing my pet on my home screen always reminds me to check up on him and fill in more journals and complete more goals.
+ There are insights so you can see how your motivation and mood fluctuated throughout the days and weeks.
+ It’s a very stress-free app that brings me a lot of happiness when I use it.

The only things I would say to improve are: 1) being able to interact with the pet more than once a day. Perhaps some mini games or conversations and such before it sleeps? And 2) being able to set specific goals of our own (or just a more varied variety, really!)

Despite that, though, those complaints still aren’t enough to rate this app any less than 5 stars. It has really helped my depression so much and I can really feel that the developers care for the users. I highly recommend!

title: Do self care for the screen pet’s sake!
body: It strange how I can’t keep up with self care because I matter but I can do it because a little computerised bird needs me to so that it gets looked after! Seriously though, lovely and intuitive little app. It has some brilliant prompts for self reflection, life improvement, and daily self care, including picking up on words you say to ask you questions about later. Sometimes it misunderstands the context you used the word in which can lead to some funny responses from it (for example it will assume any name you mentioned is a person in your life who it can ask you further questions about, or if you say ‘I am grateful that I am in less pain today’ it will tell you later that today you were grateful for pain!) but that only really makes me laugh and isn’t a serious negative. I’m confident that any genuine issues will be ironed out in time because the creators seem to really care about making a good and helpful app and do seem to be listening and interacting with their users. I’ve not found anything myself that is more than a slight niggle in my overall enjoyment of the app.
